The '''2024–25 season''' was [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]]'s 33rd season in the [[Premier League]], their [[List of Arsenal F.C. seasons|99th consecutive season]] in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of English football, and 108th season in the top flight overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |title=All-time Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 Jun 2013 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jun 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622042610/https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |title=English Clubs Divisional Movements 1888–2016 |last1=Ross |first1=James |last2=Heneghan |first2=Michael |last3=Orford |first3=Stuart |last4=Culliton |first4=Eoin |date=25 Aug 2016 |website=[[RSSSF|Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |access-date=8 Jun 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622041929/https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref> In addition to the [[2024–25 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal also participated in this season's editions of the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], the latter of which was their [[Arsenal F.C. in European football|39th European campaign]]. The season covers the period from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025.

Managed by [[Mikel Arteta]] in his fifth full season, Arsenal finished as Premier League runners-up for the third consecutive campaign and reached the semi-finals of the Champions League for the first time since [[2008–09 Arsenal F.C. season|2008–09]].

==Review==
===Background===
{{See also|2023–24 Arsenal F.C. season}}
The 2023–24 campaign was a record-breaking season for Arsenal.<ref name="2023–24 season AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/records-we-broke-and-milestones-hit-2324 |title=The records we broke and milestones hit in 23/24 |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=20 May 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref> They kicked off their campaign by winning the [[2023 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] for the 17th time in their history.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fa-community-shield-match-report-trossard-penalty-shootout |title=Report: Arsenal 1–1 Man City (4–1 pens) |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=6 Aug 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref>

The Gunners were the third-youngest team in the [[2023–24 Premier League]] with an average starting age of 25 years and 158 days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-analysed-9-reasons-why-we-shined-2324 |title=Arsenal Analysed: 9 reasons why we shined in 23/24 |last=Clarke |first=Adrian |date=23 May 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref> They scored 91 goals in the Premier League, their highest-ever total in the competition. It was the most they had netted in a league campaign since [[1952–53 Arsenal F.C. season|1952–53]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/113-goals-stats-behind-our-incredible-haul |title=113 goals! The stats behind our incredible haul |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=22 May 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref> Arteta's side conceded just 29 goals in the Premier League – five fewer than the second-lowest team. This was Arsenal's best defensive record for 20 years. They finished with a goal difference of +62 in the division, their highest-ever total in the competition's history. The Gunners kept 18 [[clean sheet]]s (7 at home, 11 on the road) in the league, five more than the second-highest sides.<ref name="2023–24 season AFC"/>

Arsenal won 28 Premier League games in the 2023–24 season, their highest tally in a top-flight campaign since [[1970–71 Arsenal F.C. season|1970–71]]. The Gunners picked up 89 points, the second-highest total in their history.<ref name="2023–24 season AFC"/> However, this was still not enough to win the Premier League title. Arteta's side ended their season as runners-up – the third-best second-placed team in the competition's history – two points behind champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5495587/2024/05/19/premier-league-points-total-second-place-arsenal/ |title=How the number of points required to win the Premier League title has gone up and up |last=Rose |first=Ajay |date=19 May 2024 |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref>

After a six-year absence, Arsenal started their 20th UEFA Champions League campaign since the [[1992–93 UEFA Champions League|1992–93 season]] in September 2023. They finished the group stage as winners of Group B, with the highest goal difference of any team (+12).<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Football on TNT Sports |author-link=TNT Sports (United Kingdom) |user=footballontnt |number=1735291298066702833 |date=14 Dec 2023 |title=Arsenal end the Champions League group stage with the highest goal difference of any team (+12) 🔥 Not bad for their first #UCL campaign in six years... |access-date=8 Jun 2024}}</ref> The Gunners progressed to the quarter-final of the Champions League for the first time since [[2009–10 Arsenal F.C. season|2009–10]], ending a run of seven consecutive last-16 eliminations in the competition.<ref name="2023–24 season AFC"/> Their first Champions League campaign in seven years finished in the last eight, after a 3–2 aggregate loss to German side [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].

===Pre-season===
The [[UEFA Euro 2024]] took place in Germany from 14 June to 14 July. Ten Arsenal players (excluding loaned out players) were named in [[UEFA Euro 2024 squads|squads]] for the tournament: [[Leandro Trossard]] (Belgium), [[Aaron Ramsdale]], [[Declan Rice]] and [[Bukayo Saka]] (England), [[William Saliba]] (France), [[Kai Havertz]] (Germany), [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]] (Italy), [[Jakub Kiwior]] (Poland), [[David Raya]] (Spain), and [[Oleksandr Zinchenko (footballer)|Oleksandr Zinchenko]] (Ukraine).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/when-our-11-gunners-will-be-playing-euro-2024 |title=When our 11 Gunners will be playing at Euro 2024 |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=14 Jun 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Jul 2024}}</ref> Raya became a Euro 2024 winner as Spain beat England in the final.<ref name="Raya won Euro AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/raya-wins-euro-2024-spain |title=David Raya wins Euro 2024 with Spain |date=14 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=15 Jul 2024}}</ref>

[[Gabriel Magalhães]] and [[Gabriel Martinelli]] were named in Brazil's squad for the [[2024 Copa América]], held in the United States from 20 June to 14 July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/copa-america-2024-our-guide-brazils-chances |title=Copa America 2024: Our guide to Brazil's chances |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=20 Jun 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Jul 2024}}</ref> Brazil were eliminated in the quarter-finals on 6 July.

On 24 June, Arsenal announced that Estonian goalkeeper and [[Arsenal F.C. Under-21s and Academy|academy]] graduate [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] had signed a new contract.<ref name="Hein new contract AFC"/><ref name="Hein new contract NYT"/>

It was reported on 15 July that the first-team players who had not been away on international duty at Euro 2024 or Copa América were back to the [[Arsenal Training Centre|London Colney training ground]] for pre-season training.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/boys-are-back-training-all-best-photos |title=The boys are back in training! All the best photos |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=15 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Jul 2024}}</ref>

On 21 July, manager Arteta named an initial 26-man squad – including 12 academy players – for the trip to the United States where they would play three friendlies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-name-26-man-squad-us-tour |title=Arsenal name 26-man squad for US Tour |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=21 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=21 Jul 2024}}</ref>

Three days later, Arsenal faced Premier League side [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] at [[Dignity Health Sports Park]] in [[Carson, California|Carson]], California. [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] gave the Gunners a first-half lead with a volley. The Cherries equalised through a deflected [[Antoine Semenyo]] effort in the second half. Following the game, a pre-planned [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] took place, which saw Arteta's side triumph 5–4 with Kiwior netting the winning spot-kick after Hein made two saves.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5655378/2024/07/25/arsenal-bournemouth-friendly-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 1 Bournemouth 1: Implications of Smith Rowe exit, Vieira scores, Nwaneri impresses |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=25 Jul 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=25 Jul 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Jul-25/arsenal-bournemouth-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–1 Bournemouth (5–4 pens) |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=25 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=25 Jul 2024}}</ref>

On 27 July, the Gunners took on Premier League club [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[SoFi Stadium]], the home of the [[National Football League]]'s [[Los Angeles Rams]] which is also owned by [[Kroenke Sports and Entertainment]]. [[Rasmus Højlund]] gave United an early lead. [[Gabriel Jesus]] levelled for Arteta's side with a close-range finish. Substitute Martinelli scored a late goal, helping Arsenal win 2–1. In the post-match penalty shootout, United won 4–3 following misses from Havertz and Kiwior.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5659074/2024/07/27/arsenal-man-united-friendly-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 2 Man United 1: Goals for Jesus and Martinelli, Nwaneri impresses again |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=27 Jul 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=28 Jul 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Jul-28/arsenal-manchester-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–1 Manchester United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=28 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=28 Jul 2024}}</ref>

Arsenal played their third and final game of the 10-day USA tour against Premier League side [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Lincoln Financial Field]] in [[Philadelphia]] on 31 July. Goals from [[Mohamed Salah]] and [[Fábio Carvalho (footballer, born 2002)|Fábio Carvalho]] gave Liverpool a 2–0 lead. The Gunners pulled one back through Havertz's close-range shot, but they were unable to find an equaliser. After the game, Arteta's team flew back to London overnight.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/700488 |title=Liverpool edge Arsenal in front of historic Philadelphia crowd |last=Olley |first=James |date=1 Aug 2024 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=1 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Jul-31/liverpool-2-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Liverpool 2–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5674448/2024/08/02/arsenal-us-tour-calafiori-scramble-young-v-old-table-tennis-and-justin-bieber/ |title=Arsenal's U.S. tour: Calafiori scramble, 'young vs old' table tennis – and Justin Bieber |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=2 Aug 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=2 Aug 2024}}</ref>

On 6 August, the club confirmed that Zinchenko would wear the number 17 shirt, moving from his previous number 35.<ref name="Zinchenko No 17 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/oleksandr-zinchenko-gets-new-squad-number |title=Oleksandr Zinchenko gets new squad number |date=6 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=6 Aug 2024}}</ref>

The Gunners continued their preparations for the new season with a 4–1 win over reigning [[Bundesliga]] [[2023–24 Bundesliga|champions]] [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] at [[Emirates Stadium]] on 7 August. Zinchenko, Trossard and Gabriel Jesus all scored in the first half. Havertz then added a fourth after half-time. [[Xabi Alonso]]'s side claimed a late consolation through [[Adam Hložek]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/707619 |title=Arsenal thrash Bayer Leverkusen as Xhaka makes Emirates return |date=7 Aug 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=8 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Aug-07/arsenal-4-1-bayer-04-leverkusen-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 4–1 Bayer Leverkusen |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=7 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Aug 2024}}</ref>

[[File:2024 Emirates Cup - Riccardo Calafiori (2).jpg|thumb|right|150px|New recruit Riccardo Calafiori warming up in the 2024 Emirates Cup match]]
Arsenal finished their pre-season campaign by beating [[Ligue 1]] side [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] 2–0 to claim the [[2024 Emirates Cup]] on 11 August. Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães both scored from Rice corners in the first half. New signing [[Riccardo Calafiori]] made his non-competitive debut for the Gunners as a substitute in the 64th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-lyon/report/508035 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Lyon: Riccardo Calafiori makes Gunners debut as William Saliba and Gabriel both score from corners |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=11 Aug 2024 |website=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=12 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Aug-11/arsenal-olympique-lyonnais-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–0 Lyon |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=11 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 Aug 2024}}</ref>

====First-team transfers (summer transfer window)====
The Premier League [[List of English football transfers summer 2024|summer transfer window]] ran from 14 June to 30 August 2024.<ref name="Transfer windows PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4012986 |title=Dates for summer 2024 and winter 2025 transfer windows confirmed |date=15 May 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=15 May 2024}}</ref> Arsenal announced on 3 June that they were to release 22 players,<ref name="Retained List"/> two of whom, [[Mohamed Elneny]] and [[Cédric Soares]], had made 161 and 64 appearances for the Gunners' first-team in all competitions respectively.

[[File:RC Lens - Arsenal FC (03-10-2023) 21 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|150px|David Raya playing for Arsenal in October 2023]]
On 4 July, the club confirmed that they had completed the permanent signing of 28-year-old Spanish goalkeeper and reigning [[Premier League Golden Glove]] winner [[David Raya]] from Premier League side [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on a long-term deal after the Spaniard's initial loan spell with the Gunners in 2023–24.<ref name="Raya joined AFC"/> The transfer fee was reported to be [[Pound sterling|£]]27&nbsp;million.<ref name="Raya fee"/> He is the fifteenth player from Spain to represent Arsenal's first team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/quiz-name-every-spaniard-play-arsenal |title=Quiz: Name every Spaniard to play for Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=4 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=4 Jul 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240704165229/https://www.arsenal.com/news/quiz-name-every-spaniard-play-arsenal |archive-date=4 Jul 2024}}</ref>

On 15 July, the Gunners announced the departures of two first-team players: Belgian midfielder [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] joined [[La Liga]] club [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on a season-long loan,<ref name="Sambi Lokonga loaned out AFC"/> and Portuguese defender [[Nuno Tavares]] joined [[Serie A]] side [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] on a one-year loan.<ref name="Tavares loaned out AFC"/>

Arsenal confirmed on 29 July that 22-year-old Italian defender [[Riccardo Calafiori]] had joined the club on a long-term contract from Serie A side [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]],<ref name="Calafiori joined AFC"/> for a reported fee of an initial £33.6&nbsp;million ([[Euro|€]]40&nbsp;million), which could reach £42&nbsp;million (€50&nbsp;million) with add-ons.<ref name="Calafiori fee"/> He would wear the number 33 shirt,<ref name="Calafiori joined AFC"/> and would be the fourth Italian to feature for the Gunners in competitive action.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/15-facts-you-need-know-about-riccardo-calafiori |title=15 facts you need to know about Riccardo Calafiori |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 Jul 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=29 Jul 2024}}</ref>

On 2 August, the club announced that English midfielder and academy graduate [[Emile Smith Rowe]], who had made 115 first-team appearances in all competitions for the Gunners, joined Premier League side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on a permanent transfer.<ref name="Smith Rowe departed AFC"/> The fee was reported to be an initial £27&nbsp;million, potentially rising to £34&nbsp;million in add-ons.<ref name="Smith Rowe fee"/>

The Gunners confirmed on 13 August that Estonian goalkeeper [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] had joined La Liga side [[Real Valladolid]] on a one-year loan.<ref name="Hein loaned out AFC"/>

[[File:Miker Merino 2018 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|150px|Mikel Merino with Real Sociedad in 2018]]
On 27 August, Arsenal announced that 28-year-old Spanish midfielder and Euro 2024 winner [[Mikel Merino]] had joined the club from La Liga side [[Real Sociedad]] on a long-term contract.<ref name="Merino joined AFC"/> The transfer fee was reported to be an initial £27.4&nbsp;million (€32.5&nbsp;million), with a further £4.2&nbsp;million (€5&nbsp;million) in add-ons.<ref name="Merino contract & fee"/> He would take the number 23 shirt,<ref name="Merino joined AFC"/> and would be the sixteenth Spaniard to play for Arsenal's first team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/quiz-name-every-spaniard-play-arsenal |title=Quiz: Name every Spaniard to play for Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=27 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Aug 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240828044812/https://www.arsenal.com/news/quiz-name-every-spaniard-play-arsenal |archive-date=28 Aug 2024}}</ref>

On 28 August, the club confirmed the loan departure of Portuguese midfielder [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] to [[Primeira Liga]] side [[FC Porto|Porto]] until the end of the season.<ref name="Vieira loaned out AFC"/>

On English transfer deadline day, 30 August, Arsenal announced that the club had signed 35-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]] on a season-long loan from Premier League side Bournemouth. He would take the number 32 shirt.<ref name="Neto joined AFC"/> On the night 29-year-old English forward [[Raheem Sterling]] joined Arsenal on a one-year loan from Premier League club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] after a deal sheet was submitted to allow his move to go through beyond the transfer deadline.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/13206204/raheem-sterling-chelsea-winger-joins-arsenal-on-season-long-loan-after-stamford-bridge-exile |title=Raheem Sterling: Chelsea winger joins Arsenal on season-long loan after Stamford Bridge exile |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=31 Aug 2024}}</ref> He would wear the number 30 shirt.<ref name="Sterling No 30 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/raheem-sterling-given-squad-number |title=Raheem Sterling given squad number |date=3 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 Sep 2024}}</ref>

On the same day, the Gunners confirmed the departures of three first-team players: English Goalkeeper [[Aaron Ramsdale]] joined Premier League side [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on a permanent transfer for a reported fee of £18&nbsp;million with £7&nbsp;million in add-ons.<ref name="Ramsdale fee"/><ref name="Ramsdale departed AFC"/> English striker and academy graduate [[Eddie Nketiah]], who had made 168 first-team appearances in all competitions for the Gunners, joined Premier League club [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on a permanent deal.<ref name="Nketiah departed AFC"/> The fee was reported to be an initial £25&nbsp;million, potentially rising to £30&nbsp;million in add-ons.<ref name="Nketiah fee"/> English forward and academy graduate [[Reiss Nelson]] joined Premier League side Fulham on a season-long loan.<ref name="Nelson loaned out AFC"/>

After the summer transfer window closed, there were twenty-two players in the first-team squad: two goalkeepers, nine defenders, six midfielders, and five forwards. Six other first-team players were out on loan.<ref name="first-team squad (Sep) AFC"/>

===August===
Arteta's side kicked off their Premier League campaign with a 2–0 win over [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at home on 17 August. Havertz headed in a 25th-minute opener from Saka's cross before the roles were reversed on 74 minutes as Saka picked up Havertz's pass and rifled into the near post. Arsenal goalkeeper Raya made two vital saves to keep out [[Jørgen Strand Larsen]]'s close-range header and [[Pablo Sarabia]]'s first-time volley.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Aug-17/arsenal-2-0-wolves-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–0 Wolves |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=17 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=18 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v WOL PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5704913/2024/08/17/arsenal-wolves-result-analysis-report/ |title=Arsenal 2 Wolves 0 – Did Saka settle into the season quickly? How good was Raya's save? |last=Campbell |first=Jordan |date=17 Aug 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=18 Aug 2024}}</ref> The result meant that the Gunners had scored in each of their last 34 meetings with Wolves in all competitions, the longest scoring streak against an opponent in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4082452 |title=Saka stars for Arsenal in opening win against Wolves |date=17 Aug 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=18 Aug 2024}}</ref>

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3 formation]]) for Premier League away match against Aston Villa on 24 August<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/115837 |title=Aston Villa v Arsenal, 2024/25 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=24 Aug 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=25 Aug 2024}}</ref>
}}
On 24 August, Arsenal played their first away game of the season against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], the only side to complete the league double over the Gunners in the previous campaign. The hosts thought they had taken the lead on 54 minutes when [[Amadou Onana]]'s deflected shot looped up onto the crossbar, with the rebound falling for an unmarked [[Ollie Watkins]] to head home from close range, only for Arsenal goalkeeper Raya to get off the ground to make a stunning one-handed stop,<ref name="AVL v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/aston-villa-vs-arsenal/report/505817 |title=Aston Villa 0–2 Arsenal: Leandro Trossard and Thomas Partey on target as Gunners claim revenge |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=24 Aug 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=25 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref name="AVL v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4090903 |title=Trossard stars off the bench to maintain winning start for Arsenal |date=24 Aug 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=25 Aug 2024}}</ref><ref name="AVL v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Aug-24/aston-villa-0-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Aston Villa 0–2 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=24 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=25 Aug 2024}}</ref> which would later win August 2024's [[Premier League Save of the Month]] award.<ref name="Raya won August's PL SOTM"/> Substitute Trossard broke the deadlock in the 67th minute, sweeping home with his first touch. Partey scored his first away goal in the Premier League on 77 minutes with a long-range effort. Two minutes later, manager Arteta sent on new signing Calafiori for his Gunners debut. The 2–0 win meant that Arsenal had won their first two games in a top-flight campaign without conceding for the third time in their history, after previously doing so in [[1924–25 Arsenal F.C. season|1924–25]] and [[1971–72 Arsenal F.C. season|1971–72]].<ref name="AVL v ARS PL"/>

On 30 August, Arsenal announced that new recruit [[Mikel Merino]], who joined the club just three days prior, suffered a shoulder injury in his first training session with the team. He would be out of action for a few weeks.<ref name="Merino suffered injury AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/merino-miss-brighton-game-through-injury |title=Merino to miss Brighton game through injury |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=30 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Aug 2024}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus and [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]] were also out injured.<ref name="Merino suffered injury AFC"/>

Ahead of the first international break of the season, the Gunners played at home against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on 31 August. Arteta was forced to name four academy players on the bench because deadline-day signings [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]] and [[Raheem Sterling]] were not registered in time to play in this match and there were no other fit senior players up until that point.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-trossard-returns-against-brighton |title=Team News: Trossard returns against Brighton |last=James |first=Josh |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Sep 2024}}</ref> Arsenal controlled the first half and took the lead in the 38th minute as Havertz lobbed the onrushing goalkeeper from outside of the box.<ref name="ARS v BHA PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5726081/2024/08/31/arsenal-brighton-premier-league-result-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 1 Brighton 1: Explaining Rice's red as Arteta's side drop points in the title race – The Briefing |last=de Roché |first=Art |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=1 Sep 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BHA PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Aug-31/arsenal-1-1-brighton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–1 Brighton |last=James |first=Josh |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Sep 2024}}</ref> But the game completely changed four minutes into the second half when Rice was shown the first red card of his career by referee [[Chris Kavanagh (referee)|Chris Kavanagh]], after the midfielder received a controversial second yellow card for "delaying" [[Joël Veltman]]'s free-kick near the touchline deep in Brighton's half.<ref name="ARS v BHA PL NYT"/><ref name="ARS v BHA PL AFC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13207688/declan-rice-red-card-five-reasons-arsenal-midfielder-was-right-to-be-shocked-at-brighton-red-card |title=Declan Rice red card: Five reasons Arsenal midfielder was right to be 'shocked' at Brighton red card |last=Walker |first=Ron |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Sep 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/41067862/rice-red-card-sets-arsenal-back-busy-transfer-window |title=Rice red card sets Arsenal back despite busy transfer window |last=Olley |first=James |date=31 Aug 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=1 Sep 2024}}</ref> The visitors equalised on 58 minutes as Pedro tucked home the rebound after Raya saved [[Yankuba Minteh]]'s shot. 10-man Arsenal fought hard to prevent conceding another goal and the game ended 1–1.<ref name="ARS v BHA PL NYT"/><ref name="ARS v BHA PL AFC"/>

===September===
Twelve Arsenal players (excluding players who were loaned out) were named in their respective countries' senior squads for [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international fixtures]] in September: Gabriel Magalhães (Brazil), Rice and Saka (England), Saliba (France), Partey (as Ghana's captain),<ref name="Partey as Ghana's captain">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/pidgin/articles/cdx67y52dxko |title=Milson last minute goal upset Ghana for 2025 Afcon qualifiers against Angola |date=5 Sep 2024 |work=[[BBC News Pidgin]] |access-date=6 Sep 2024}}</ref><ref name="Partey as Ghana's captain 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/pidgin/articles/ckgwq22qle5o |title=Sako equalizer put Ghana for tight position for 2025 Afcon qualifiers |date=9 Sep 2024 |work=BBC News Pidgin |access-date=10 Sep 2024}}</ref> Havertz (Germany), Calafiori (Italy), [[Jurriën Timber]] (Netherlands), [[Martin Ødegaard]] (as Norway's captain), Kiwior (Poland), Raya (Spain), and Zinchenko (Ukraine).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/when-our-12-internationals-will-be-action |title=When our 12 internationals will be in action |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 Sep 2024}}</ref>

On 4 September, the club submitted their 2024–25 Champions League squad for the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League league phase|league phase]] of the competition. Twenty-two first-team players and young goalkeeper [[Tommy Setford]] who joined Arsenal's academy from Dutch side [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in July 2024,<ref name="Setford joined AFC"/> were registered on the Squad List A.<ref name="UCL squad AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-select-2425-champions-league-squad |title=Arsenal select 24/25 Champions League squad |date=4 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Sep 2024}}</ref> Nine days later, the club confirmed that 22 first-team players and 48 under-21 players were registered on the 2024–25 Premier League Squad List for the first half of the season.<ref name="PL squad AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-submit-202425-premier-league-squad-list |title=Arsenal submit 2024/25 Premier League squad list |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=13 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=13 Sep 2024}}</ref>

Arsenal announced on 12 September that manager Arteta had signed a new contract with the club,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mikel-arteta-signs-new-arsenal-contract |title=Mikel Arteta signs new Arsenal contract |date=12 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 Sep 2024}}</ref> reportedly keeping him at Emirates Stadium until 2027.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5714657/2024/09/12/mikel-arteta-new-arsenal-contract/ |title=Mikel Arteta agrees new three-year Arsenal contract |last=Ornstein |first=David |date=12 Sep 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=12 Sep 2024}}</ref> A day later, Arsenal confirmed that Ødegaard suffered an ankle injury during Norway's game against Austria on 9 September, and Calafiori also returned from Italy duty with a calf injury.<ref name="Ødegaard suffered injury AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/artetas-odegaard-injury-update-ahead-tottenham |title=Arteta's Odegaard injury update ahead of Tottenham |date=13 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Sep 2024}}</ref>

| GK_nat = ESP | GK = Raya
| RB_nat = ENG | RB = White

| caption = Starting XI ([[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]]) for Premier League away match against Tottenham Hotspur on 15 September<ref name="TOT v ARS PL 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/115865 |title=Spurs v Arsenal, 2024/25 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=15 Sep 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Sep 2024}}</ref>
}}
The Gunners continued their Premier League campaign with a [[North London derby]] away against 10th-placed [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on 15 September.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Sep-15/tottenham-hotspur-0-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Tottenham Hotspur 0–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Sep 2024}}</ref> Arteta faced a sudden lack of midfield options and was forced to name five academy players on the bench, because six first-team players were injured up until that point and Rice was suspended for the game.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-jorginho-one-two-changes-spurs |title=Team news: Jorginho one of two changes at Spurs |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Sep 2024}}</ref> In the 64th minute, Gabriel Magalhães netted the only goal of the game with a header from Saka's corner, becoming the fourth Arsenal player to score 10+ headed goals in the Premier League.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4109079 |title=Gabriel header earns derby win to send Arsenal second |date=15 Sep 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Sep 2024}}</ref> New loan signing Sterling made his debut for Arsenal as a substitute on 80 minutes.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL AFC"/> The 1–0 win meant that the Gunners had won six consecutive Premier League away matches for the first time since 2013, and they had won three consecutive away North London derbies for the first time since 1988. The result sent them back to the second of the Premier League table.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL"/>

Arsenal opened their 2024–25 Champions League campaign in [[Bergamo]], Italy, facing the previous season's [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] champions [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] on 19 September. In the 48th minute with the score at 0–0, the hosts were awarded a penalty after Partey had fouled [[Éderson (footballer, born 1999)|Éderson]]. However, Raya made a brilliant double save to keep out [[Mateo Retegui]]'s attempt and follow-up header.<ref name="ATA v ARS UCL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5773783/2024/09/19/atalanta-arsenal-raya-champions-league/ |title=Atalanta 0 Arsenal 0 – Raya's brilliance, Odegaard missed and is Serie A posing a threat? |last1=de Roché |first1=Art |last2=Carey |first2=Mark |last3=Horncastle |first3=James |date=19 Sep 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=20 Sep 2024}}</ref> He became the fourth Arsenal goalkeeper to save a penalty in the Champions League, after [[Richard Wright (footballer)|Richard Wright]], [[Jens Lehmann]] and [[Łukasz Fabiański]].<ref name="ATA v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Sep-19/atalanta-bergamasca-calcio-0-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Atalanta 0–0 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=19 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=20 Sep 2024}}</ref> The game ended goalless.<ref name="ATA v ARS UCL NYT"/>

The Gunners played their third consecutive away game in seven days against 1st-placed Manchester City on 22 September. [[Erling Haaland]] opened the scoring early on for the hosts. Arteta's side drew level with a long-range stunner scored by Calafiori, then took the lead through a Gabriel Magalhães header. However, in the final seconds of the first half, Trossard was given a controversial second yellow card for "kicking the ball away and delaying a restart" by referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]].<ref name="MCI v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Sep-22/manchester-city-2-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Man City 2–2 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=22 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Sep 2024}}</ref><ref name="MCI v ARS PL ESPN">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704325 |title=Man City score 98th-minute equaliser against 10-man Arsenal |date=22 Sep 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=23 Sep 2024}}</ref> It was later revealed by broadcaster [[Sky Sports]] that there was just 0.84 seconds between Oliver's whistle and Trossard kicking the ball way.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/watch/video/sports/football/13220602/man-city-v-arsenal-was-leandro-trossard-hard-done-by |title=Man City v Arsenal {{pipe}} Was Leandro Trossard hard done by? |date=23 Sep 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=23 Sep 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.givemesport.com/things-you-may-have-missed-from-man-city-vs-arsenal/ |title=Things you may have Missed from Man City vs Arsenal |last=Altimas |first=Callum |date=23 Sep 2024 |website=givemesport.com |access-date=23 Sep 2024}}</ref> 10-man Arsenal battled hard in the second half until the eighth minute of stoppage time when [[John Stones]] latched onto a rebound and netted an equaliser for the hosts.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL ESPN"/> The game also saw academy player [[Myles Lewis-Skelly]] make his senior debut for the Gunners as a substitute in the second half.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL AFC"/> In the post-match press conference, Arteta confirmed that White came on to help the team for the second-half despite being injured.<ref name="White suffered injury football.london">{{cite web |url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/news/arsenal-boss-mikel-arteta-confirms-29986311 |title=Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta confirms Ben White injury truth after Man City thriller |last=Holland |first=Josh |date=22 Sep 2024 |website=football.london |access-date=23 Sep 2024}}</ref>

Arsenal's 2024–25 EFL Cup campaign began in the third round against [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] at home on 25 September.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Sep-25/arsenal-bolton-wanderers-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 5–1 Bolton Wanderers |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=25 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=26 Sep 2024}}</ref> Arteta opted to rest several first-team players and chose a youthful line-up with an average age of 23 years and 87 days – the youngest starting XI the Spaniard has named in his near-five-year spell as Gunners boss.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/stats-and-records-around-our-latest-debutants |title=The stats and records around our latest debutants |last=James |first=Josh |date=26 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Sep 2024}}</ref> With number one stopper Raya and 18-year-old understudy Tommy Setford injured and summer loan signing Neto cup-tied,<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bolton-wanderers/report/521490 |title=Arsenal 5–1 Bolton: Ethan Nwaneri scores twice and Raheem Sterling nets first Gunners goal as League One side swiped away |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=25 Sep 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=26 Sep 2024}}</ref> Arteta called on Arsenal's fourth choice [[Jack Porter (footballer)|Jack Porter]], who at 16 years and 72 days became the youngest goalkeeper to play for Arsenal's first team,<ref name="Porter youngest GK AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/get-know-jack-porter-record-breaking-keeper |title=Get to know Jack Porter – a record-breaking keeper |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=25 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=25 Sep 2024}}</ref> and the youngest player to start an Arsenal first-team match.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC"/> Another debutant [[Josh Nichols]] also received his first start.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC"/> Rice put the Gunners ahead on 16 minutes. [[Ethan Nwaneri]] netted his first two senior goals for Arsenal in the 37th and 49th minute respectively,<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup AFC"/> becoming the youngest player to score for the club's first team since 2008, and to notch a brace since 2004.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC"/> [[Aaron Collins (footballer)|Aaron Collins]] pulled one back for Bolton on 53 minutes. Sterling netted his first Arsenal goal in the 64th minute.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup SkySports"/> Defender [[Maldini Kacurri]] made his senior debut as a substitute in the 70th minute, becoming the first Albanian national to represent Arsenal's first team in the club's history.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC"/> Havertz wrapped up the scoring on 77 minutes.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup AFC"/> Young winger [[Ismeal Kabia]] received his debut in the 81st minute.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup debutants AFC"/> The 5–1 result advanced Arsenal to the next round.<ref name="ARS v BOL EFLCup SkySports"/>

On 28 September, Arteta's side played at home against newly promoted [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. Martinelli opened the scoring for Arsenal, ending his 19-game goal drought dating back to 4 March. Trossard doubled the lead on the stroke of half-time.<ref name="ARS v LEI PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Sep-28/arsenal-4-2-leicester-city-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 4–2 Leicester City |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=28 Sep 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=29 Sep 2024}}</ref> But [[James Justin]]'s deflected header and first-time volley after the interval brought Leicester back level. The Gunners restored their two-goal advantage in second-half stoppage time through a [[Wilfred Ndidi]] [[own goal]] and a Havertz strike. The game ended 4–2.<ref name="ARS v LEI PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4130146 |title=Arsenal snatch LATE victory to go level with Man City |date=28 Sep 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=29 Sep 2024}}</ref>

===October===

| RB_nat = NED | RB = Timber

| caption = Starting XI (4–4–2) for Champions League home match against Paris Saint-Germain on 1 October<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/lineups/_/gameId/720443 |title=Arsenal 2–0 PSG (Oct 1, 2024) Lineups |date=1 Oct 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=2 Oct 2024}}</ref>
}}
Arsenal returned to Champions League action on 1 October, hosting the previous season's [[2023–24 Ligue 1|Ligue 1]] champions and [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] semi-finalists [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. The Gunners took the lead in the 20th minute through Havertz.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-LP AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-01/arsenal-2-0-paris-saint-germain-fc-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–0 PSG |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Oct 2024}}</ref> Fifteen minutes later, Saka curled a low free-kick from wide on the right into a crowded penalty area; the ball somehow evaded everyone and flew straight into the back of the net.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-LP SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-paris-saint-germain/report/521617 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Paris Saint-Germain: Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka score as Gunners claim Champions League win |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=1 Oct 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=2 Oct 2024}}</ref> It was Arsenal's first direct free-kick goal in the Champions League since November 2002.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-LP AFC"/> In the 64th minute Arteta handed a belated debut to summer signing Merino who had recovered from a shoulder injury.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-LP SkySports"/> The game ended 2–0.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-LP SkySports"/>

Ahead of the second international break of the campaign, Arteta's men played their seventh match in 21 days on 5 October when they faced newly promoted [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at home. Second-half goals from Havertz, Martinelli and Saka saw the Gunners come from behind to win 3–1 and extend their unbeaten start to the season to ten games.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-05/arsenal-3-1-southampton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-1 Southampton |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=5 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=6 Oct 2024}}</ref> This was Arsenal's 400th Premier League home victory, making them the second side to reach the milestone.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4138697 |title=Saka stars in Arsenal comeback win over Southampton |date=5 Oct 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=6 Oct 2024}}</ref> Havertz became the first Arsenal player to score in seven consecutive home appearances in all competitions since [[2011–12 Arsenal F.C. season|2011–12]].<ref name="ARS v SOU PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v SOU PL"/>

Ten Arsenal players (excluding loaned out players) joined up with their respective senior national teams for international fixtures in October: Trossard (Belgium), Gabriel Magalhães and Martinelli (Brazil), Rice and Saka (England), Saliba (France), Calafiori (Italy), Kiwior (Poland), Merino and Raya (Spain).<ref name="Intl call-ups Oct 2024 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/whos-playing-and-when-international-break |title=Who's playing and when in the international break? |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=7 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Oct 2024}}</ref>

Arsenal faced 13th-placed Bournemouth away on 19 October.<ref name="BOU v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-19/bournemouth-2-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Bournemouth 2–0 Arsenal |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=19 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=20 Oct 2024}}</ref> Already missing Ødegaard and Saka through injury, the Gunners lost Saliba in the 30th minute as the French centre-back was shown the first red card of his career for a foul on [[Evanilson (footballer, born 1999)|Evanilson]] near the halfway line after a poor backwards pass from Trossard.<ref name="BOU v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="Saliba red card SI">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/arsenal-william-saliba-red-card-vs-bournemouth-draws-controversy |title=Arsenal's William Saliba Red Card vs. Bournemouth Draws Controversy |last=Mallow |first=Max |date=19 Oct 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=20 Oct 2024}}</ref><ref name="BOU v ARS PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5855342/2024/10/20/arsenal-bournemouth-saliba-kiwior-arteta/ |title=In Arsenal's quest for perfection, the small errors carry big consequences |last=de Roché |first=Art |date=20 Oct 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=20 Oct 2024}}</ref> Saliba was initially given a yellow card, but the referee upgraded his decision to a red after being instructed to check the pitchside monitor by [[video assistant referee]] [[Jarred Gillett]].<ref name="BOU v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="Saliba red card SI"/> Martinelli missed a golden chance to put 10-man Arsenal in front on 69 minutes, shooting straight at the Bournemouth goalkeeper from close range.<ref name="BOU v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="BOU v ARS PL NYT"/> Just a minute later, [[Ryan Christie]] broke the deadlock with a first-time shot following a Bournemouth corner routine. Kiwior's loose backpass on 77 minutes resulted in the hosts scoring a decisive second goal from the penalty spot.<ref name="BOU v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="BOU v ARS PL NYT"/> The 2–0 loss was Arsenal's first defeat of the season, and their first away loss in the Premier League in 2024.<ref name="BOU v ARS PL NYT"/>

Arteta's side hosted the previous season's [[2023–24 Ukrainian Premier League|Ukrainian Premier League]] champions [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in the Champions League on 22 October. In the 29th minute, Martinelli's low shot hit the post and then rebounded back into the net off Shakhtar goalkeeper [[Dmytro Riznyk]].<ref name="ARS v SHK UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-shakhtar-donetsk/report/521635 |title=Arsenal 1–0 Shakhtar Donetsk: Gunners win but Riccardo Calafiori forced off injured ahead of Liverpool clash |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=23 Oct 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=23 Oct 2024}}</ref> The Gunners had the chance to extend the lead in the final 20 minutes, as Merino's cross was handled and they were awarded a penalty after a VAR review. But Trossard's spot-kick was poor and saved by Riznyk.<ref name="ARS v SHK UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-22/arsenal-1-0-fc-shakhtar-donetsk-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–0 Shakhtar Donetsk |last=James |first=Josh |date=22 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Oct 2024}}</ref> In stoppage time Raya produced a flying save to deny [[Pedrinho (footballer, born April 1998)|Pedrinho]]'s long-range shot, helping Arsenal win 1–0.<ref name="ARS v SHK UCL SkySports"/> The result meant that the Gunners had recorded three successive clean sheets in the Champions League for the first time since 2007.<ref name="ARS v SHK UCL AFC"/>

On 27 October, the Gunners played at home against 1st-placed Liverpool.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-27/arsenal-2-2-liverpool-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–2 Liverpool |last=James |first=Josh |date=27 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=28 Oct 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v LIV PL ESPN">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704367 |title=Salah scores late to earn Liverpool 2–2 draw at Arsenal |date=27 Oct 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=28 Oct 2024}}</ref> Saka opened the scoring in the ninth minute with a near-post finish, becoming the youngest Arsenal player to net 50 Premier League goals.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5872349/2024/10/27/arsenal-liverpool-salah-saka-nunez-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 2 Liverpool 2 – Nunez keeps his cool, and was this a missed opportunity for Arteta's side? |last1=McNicholas |first1=James |last2=Evans |first2=Gregg |last3=Harris |first3=Thom |date=27 Oct 2024 |website=The New York Times |access-date=28 Oct 2024}}</ref> [[Virgil van Dijk]] levelled for Liverpool on 18 minutes with a close-range header.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL ESPN"/> Arteta's side retook the lead in the 41st minute when Merino headed home his first Arsenal goal from Rice's free-kick.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v LIV PL ESPN"/> The Gunners were undermined by injuries to key defenders Gabriel Magalhães and Timber after the break, having already been without the suspended Saliba and injured Calafiori.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v LIV PL NYT"/> The pressure on their backline was consequently mounting before Liverpool equalised through [[Mohamed Salah]] on 81 minutes.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v LIV PL NYT"/> In second-half stoppage time Gabriel Jesus bundled the ball home, but referee [[Anthony Taylor (referee)|Anthony Taylor]] had already blown for a foul by Kiwior in the build-up.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v LIV PL ESPN"/> The game ended 2–2.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL ESPN"/>

Arsenal continued their EFL Cup campaign on 30 October, facing [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] away in the fourth round.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/preston-north-end-vs-arsenal/report/522589 |title=Preston 0–3 Arsenal: Gunners book Carabao Cup quarter-final spot after Ethan Nwaneri stunner |last=Hunter |first=Laura |date=30 Oct 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=31 Oct 2024}}</ref> Arteta handed a belated debut to teenage goalkeeper Tommy Setford, who missed the third-round game against Bolton Wanderers through injury in September.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-setford-makes-debut-and-saliba-returns |title=Team News: Setford makes debut and Saliba returns |last=James |first=Josh |date=30 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=31 Oct 2024}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus opened the scoring for the Gunners, ending his 24-game goal drought dating back to 30 January.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4160240 |title=EFL Cup fourth-round review: What we learned |last=Hancock |first=Tom |date=31 Oct 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=31 Oct 2024}}</ref> Nwaneri doubled the lead with a curling effort into the top corner, becoming the youngest player to net in each of his first two starts for Arsenal.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup PL"/> Second-half substitute Havertz rounded off the scoring with a header. Young defender [[Ayden Heaven]] received his debut in the final ten minutes.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Oct-30/preston-north-end-0-3-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Preston North End 0–3 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=30 Oct 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=31 Oct 2024}}</ref> The 3–0 result advanced Arsenal to the quarter-finals.<ref name="PNE v ARS EFLCup SkySports"/>

===November===
The Gunners faced 12th-placed [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] away on 2 November. [[Alexander Isak]] scored the only goal of the game for the hosts in the 12th minute. Arsenal had good chances to draw level, with Merino's shot blocked on the line and Rice heading wide from close range in either half.<ref name="NEW v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-02/newcastle-united-1-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Newcastle United 1–0 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 Nov 2024}}</ref><ref name="NEW v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/newcastle-united-vs-arsenal/report/505902 |title=Newcastle 1–0 Arsenal: Alexander Isak header hands Mikel Arteta's side another damaging Premier League defeat |last=Shread |first=Joe |date=2 Nov 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=3 Nov 2024}}</ref> This was the first time since May 2022 that Arsenal had lost successive away matches in the Premier League.<ref name="NEW v ARS PL AFC"/> It was revealed later that Rice had suffered a broken toe in this game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42311121/chelsea-vs-arsenal-arteta-praying-no-more-injuries |title=Chelsea vs. Arsenal: Arteta 'praying' for no more injuries |last=Olley |first=James |date=10 Nov 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=11 Nov 2024}}</ref>

Arteta's men made the trip to Italy for the Champions League match against the previous season's [[2023–24 Serie A|Serie A]] champions [[Inter Milan]] on 6 November. Ødegaard returned to the bench after missing 12 Arsenal games with injury.<ref name="INT v ARS UCL line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-white-returns-inter-clash |title=Team News: White returns for Inter clash |date=6 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Nov 2024}}</ref> The Gunners had a penalty shout in the 28th minute when Merino appeared to beat Inter goalkeeper [[Yann Sommer]] to a high ball in the box and took a punch to the head in the process, but VAR decided not to overturn a no-penalty decision.<ref name="INT v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-06/inter-milan-1-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Inter Milan 1–0 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=6 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Nov 2024}}</ref><ref name="INT v ARS UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/inter-milan-vs-arsenal/report/521666 |title=Inter Milan 1–0 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's side lose again as Hakan Calhanoglu penalty settles Champions League game |last=Boswell |first=Zinny |date=7 Nov 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=7 Nov 2024}}</ref> In first-half stoppage time, the hosts were awarded a spot-kick after the ball ricocheted into Merino's arm at close range, although he did not have time to move his arm out of the way.<ref name="INT v ARS UCL AFC"/><ref name="INT v ARS UCL SkySports"/> [[Hakan Çalhanoğlu]] then scored from the penalty spot – Inter's only shot on target throughout the game.<ref name="INT v ARS UCL AFC"/> Arsenal dominated the second half but could not find a way past the hosts' defence.<ref name="INT v ARS UCL SkySports"/> The 1–0 defeat was Arsenal's third away loss in 18 days.

On 10 November, the Gunners faced 4th-placed Chelsea away in their final fixture before the third international break of the season. After a scoreless first half that saw Havertz had a goal ruled out for offside by VAR,<ref name="CHE v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-arsenal/report/505909 |title=Chelsea 1–1 Arsenal: Pedro Neto strikes after Gabriel Martinelli's opener in Stamford Bridge draw |last=Yew |first=Oliver |date=10 Nov 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=11 Nov 2024}}</ref> Martinelli put Arsenal in front on the hour mark when he tucked home a cross by Ødegaard, who made his first start since 31 August.<ref name="CHE v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-10/chelsea-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Chelsea 1–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=10 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=11 Nov 2024}}</ref> [[Pedro Neto]] slammed in from distance to drag the hosts level 10 minutes later.<ref name="CHE v ARS PL AFC"/> Arsenal squandered a golden chance in stoppage time, as Saliba played an inviting ball across the Chelsea box, but Trossard poked wide from close range, with Havertz waiting to tap home behind him.<ref name="CHE v ARS PL SkySports"/> The 1–1 draw meant that the Gunners had gone four consecutive Premier League matches without a win for the first time since April 2023.<ref name="CHE v ARS PL SkySports"/>

A run of early-season injuries for Arteta's side continued, as it was reported on 13 November that White had undergone a surgery to resolve a knee issue that he had been carrying for weeks, and would be sidelined for months.<ref name="White underwent surgery TheIndependent">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/ben-white-injury-arsenal-mikel-arteta-b2646687.html |title=Arsenal suffer new injury blow as Ben White undergoes surgery |date=13 Nov 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |access-date=14 Nov 2024}}</ref>

Ten Arsenal players (excluding players who were loaned out) joined up with their respective senior national teams for international fixtures in November: Trossard (Belgium), Gabriel Magalhães and Martinelli (Brazil), Saliba (France), Havertz (Germany), Timber (Netherlands), Kiwior (Poland), Merino and Raya (Spain), and Zinchenko (Ukraine).<ref name="Intl call-ups Nov 2024 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/international-break-whos-playing-and-when |title=International break: Who's playing and when? |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=12 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 Nov 2024}}</ref>

The Gunners played at home against 5th-placed [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on 23 November. This was Arteta's 250th game in charge of Arsenal in all competitions,<ref name="ARS v NFO PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-n-forest/report/505917 |title=Arsenal 3–0 Nottingham Forest: Bukayo Saka, Thomas Partey and Ethan Nwaneri score to end four-game league winless streak |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=23 Nov 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=24 Nov 2024}}</ref> the 10th manager to reach the milestone for the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mikel-arteta-reach-250-games-our-manager |title=Arteta to reach 250 games as manager – the stats |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=23 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=24 Nov 2024}}</ref> Goals early in each half from Saka and Partey gave the Gunners a 2–0 lead.<ref name="ARS v NFO PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-23/arsenal-3-0-nottingham-forest-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3–0 Nottingham Forest |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=23 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=24 Nov 2024}}</ref> Nwaneri netted a late goal, becoming Arsenal's second-youngest scorer in the Premier League.<ref name="ARS v NFO PL SkySports"/><ref name="ARS v NFO PL AFC"/> The win was the Gunners' 2,000th in English top-flight history, making them the second side to reach this landmark.<ref name="ARS v NFO PL SkySports"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-hit-2000-top-flight-wins-all-stats |title=Arsenal hit 2,000 top-flight wins – all the stats |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=23 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=24 Nov 2024}}</ref>

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Champions League away match against Sporting CP on 26 November<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2041994/ |title=Sporting CP vs Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=26 Nov 2024 |website=UEFA |access-date=26 Nov 2024}}</ref>
}}
On 26 November, Arsenal recorded their biggest away win in the Champions League since 2003 by thumping the previous season's [[2023–24 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]] champions [[Sporting CP]] 5–1 in [[Lisbon]], Portugal.<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/sporting-lisbon-vs-arsenal/report/521678 |title=Sporting 1–5 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's full-strength side produce statement Champions League win |last=Boswell |first=Zinny |date=26 Nov 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=27 Nov 2024}}</ref><ref name="joint-biggest UCL away win AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/club-record-matched-thanks-huge-win-sporting |title=Club record matched thanks to huge win at Sporting |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=27 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Nov 2024}}</ref> Saliba made his 100th senior appearance for the Gunners,<ref name="Saliba 100 appearances AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/saliba-reach-100-arsenal-games-against-sporting |title=Saliba reaches 100 Arsenal games in Sporting win |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=26 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Nov 2024}}</ref> and Ødegaard made his first Champions League start of the season.<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-rice-and-havertz-start-lisbon |title=Team news: Rice and Havertz start in Lisbon |date=26 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Nov 2024}}</ref> Martinelli tapped in an early opener, before Havertz finished a team goal and Gabriel Magalhães headed home a corner on the stroke of half-time.<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-26/sporting-cp-1-5-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Sporting CP 1–5 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=26 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Nov 2024}}</ref> Although [[Gonçalo Inácio]] pulled one back for Sporting shortly after the break,<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL SkySports"/> Saka's penalty and Trossard's header from a rebound secured Arsenal's victory.<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL AFC"/> This was the first time since 2008 that the Gunners had scored five or more goals in an away game in the Champions League, and was the first time since 2008 that they had had five different scorers (excluding own goals) in a major European away match.<ref name="joint-biggest UCL away win AFC"/> The win lifted Arsenal into the top eight automatic qualification positions of the Champions League league phase.<ref name="SPO v ARS UCL SkySports"/>

Arteta's side faced 14th-placed [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] away on 30 November, winning 5–2 to move up to second place in the Premier League table.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4178472 |title=Saka stars as Arsenal put five past West Ham to go second |date=30 Nov 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=1 Dec 2024}}</ref> All seven goals came in the first half – equalling the Premier League record for the highest number of goals in a first half, with Gabriel Magalhães, Trossard, Ødegaard and Havertz putting the Gunners 4–0 up after 35 minutes.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL"/> Two quickfire strikes from the hosts halved the deficit.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Nov-30/west-ham-united-2-5-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: West Ham 2–5 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=30 Nov 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Dec 2024}}</ref> Saka wrapped up the scoring with a penalty just before the break.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL"/> This was the first time in Premier League history that Arsenal have scored two first-half penalties, as Ødegaard had also dispatched from the spot.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL AFC"/>

===December===
