| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Premier League home match against Manchester United on 4 December<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/lineups/_/gameId/704410 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Man United (Dec 4, 2024) Lineups |date=4 Dec 2024 |website=ESPN |access-date=5 Dec 2024}}</ref>
}}
On 4 December, Arsenal played their 500th competitive men's first-team game at Emirates Stadium against 9th-placed Manchester United.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-play-500th-match-emirates-stadium |title=Arsenal to play 500th match at Emirates Stadium |last=James |first=Josh |date=4 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Dec 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v MUN PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-04/arsenal-2-0-manchester-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–0 Manchester United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Dec 2024}}</ref> Timber broke the deadlock on 54 minutes when he flicked Rice's corner in at the near post for his first Gunners goal.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-united/report/505937 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Man Utd: Jurrien Timber and William Saliba score from corners as Gunners close gap to Liverpool |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=4 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=5 Dec 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v MUN PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4184430 |title=Arsenal punish Man Utd from set-pieces to close gap on Liverpool |date=4 Dec 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Dec 2024}}</ref> In the 67th minute, Raya made a one-handed save at full stretch to claw away [[Matthijs de Ligt]]'s header from a free-kick.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v MUN PL"/> Arteta's side doubled their advantage in the 73rd minute, as Saka's far-post corner was headed back across by Partey, the ball bounced in off Saliba's backside.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL SkySports"/><ref name="ARS v MUN PL"/> The 2–0 win meant that Arsenal had won four consecutive league games against Manchester United for the first time in their history.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v MUN PL"/>

Arteta's side faced 6th-placed Fulham away on 8 December. Ødegaard made his 100th start as [[List of Arsenal F.C. players#Captains|Arsenal's captain]].<ref name="Ødegaard 100th start as captain AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/odegaard-captain-us-100th-time-fulham |title=Odegaard to captain us for 100th time at Fulham |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=6 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=6 Dec 2024}}</ref> [[Raúl Jiménez]] put the hosts ahead in the 11th minute. Saliba levelled for the Gunners with a close-range finish from a corner routine on 52 minutes. Saka headed home in the 88th minute, but the goal was ruled out after a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] review for offside against Martinelli in the build-up.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-08/fulham-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Fulham 1–1 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=8 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=9 Dec 2024}}</ref> The game ended 1–1.<ref name="FUL v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/fulham-vs-arsenal/report/505951 |title=Fulham 1–1 Arsenal: William Saliba scores from another Gunners corner but Mikel Arteta's side held in title race blow |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=8 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=9 Dec 2024}}</ref>

The Gunners hosted the previous season's Ligue 1 runners-up [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the Champions League on 11 December. 18-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly was handed his first Champions League start, becoming the youngest player to start for Arsenal in the competition since 2011.<ref name="ARS v ASM UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-11/arsenal-3-0-monaco-fc-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3–0 Monaco |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=11 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 Dec 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v ASM UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-monaco/report/521698 |title=Arsenal 3–0 Monaco: Bukayo Saka's double secures victory as Mikel Arteta's side close in on last 16 of Champions League |last=Yew |first=Oliver |date=11 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=12 Dec 2024}}</ref> He played a key role in Saka's opener in the first half. After the break, Saka scored again and assisted substitute Havertz, helping his side win 3–0.<ref name="ARS v ASM UCL AFC"/> The result moved Arsenal up to third in the Champions League standings.<ref name="ARS v ASM UCL SkySports"/>

Arsenal played at home against 15th-placed [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 14 December. The Gunners dominated the game and had many chances to score, especially in the first half, but failed to convert any. The match finished 0–0.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4193961 |title=Everton stand firm to damage Arsenal's title hopes |date=14 Dec 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=15 Dec 2024}}</ref><ref name="ARS v EVE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-14/arsenal-0-0-everton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0–0 Everton |last=James |first=Josh |date=14 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=15 Dec 2024}}</ref> This was Arsenal's first goalless draw at the Emirates since January 2023.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL"/>

Four days later, Arsenal hosted Premier League side [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the EFL Cup quarter-finals.<ref name="ARS v CRY EFLCup PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4199678 |title=EFL Cup quarter-finals: What we learned from Wednesday's ties |last=Hancock |first=Tom |date=19 Dec 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=19 Dec 2024}}</ref> The visitors took the lead early through a [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]] finish.<ref name="ARS v CRY EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-18/arsenal-3-2-crystal-palace-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3–2 Crystal Palace |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=18 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 Dec 2024}}</ref> The Gunners turned the game around in the second half when Gabriel Jesus scored a [[hat-trick]], ending his 367-day Emirates goal drought dating back to 17 December 2023.<ref name="ARS v CRY EFLCup PL"/> Former Arsenal player [[Eddie Nketiah]] brought one back for Palace late on.<ref name="ARS v CRY EFLCup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-crystal-palace/report/523117 |title=Arsenal 3–2 Crystal Palace: Gabriel Jesus' second-half hat-trick inspires Gunners to Carabao Cup comeback win |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=19 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=19 Dec 2024}}</ref> The 3–2 result advanced Arsenal to the semi-finals for the first time since [[2021–22 Arsenal F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref name="ARS v CRY EFLCup AFC"/>

Arteta's men crossed the capital to face Crystal Palace again in the Premier League on 21 December. They wore black armbands in remembrance of [[George Eastham]],<ref name="CRY v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-21/crystal-palace-1-5-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Crystal Palace 1–5 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=21 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Dec 2024}}</ref> who served as [[List of Arsenal F.C. players#Captains|Arsenal captain]] between 1963 and 1966 and was a member of England's [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966 World Cup]]-winning [[1966 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/george-eastham-1936-2024 |title=George Eastham 1936–2024 |date=21 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Dec 2024}}</ref> following the earlier news of his passing.<ref>{{cite news |date=21 Dec 2024 |title=World Cup-winning England international Eastham dies aged 88 |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/world-cup-winning-england-international-eastham-dies-aged-88-2024-12-21/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=22 Dec 2024}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus netted two early goals for Arsenal, either side of [[Ismaïla Sarr]]'s equaliser; while Havertz, Martinelli and Rice all found the net.<ref name="CRY v ARS PL AFC"/> Raya made several crucial saves during the game, helping the Gunners win 5–1.<ref name="CRY v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/crystal-palace-vs-arsenal/report/505969 |title=Crystal Palace 1–5 Arsenal: Gabriel Jesus scores twice as Gunners close gap on Premier League leaders Liverpool |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=21 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=22 Dec 2024}}</ref> The victory marked the final away match of 2024 for Arsenal, making them the first team in English top-flight history to score five or more goals in six different away games in all competitions across a full calendar year.<ref name="CRY v ARS PL OptaAnalyst">{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/2024/12/crystal-palace-vs-arsenal-stats-premier-league |title=Crystal Palace 1–5 Arsenal Stats: Five-Star Gunners Fire Warning to Title Rivals |last=Benson |first=Ryan |date=21 Dec 2024 |website=[[Opta Sports|Opta Analyst]] |access-date=22 Dec 2024}}</ref> The result also meant that the Gunners became the first side to remain unbeaten in Premier League London derbies in a single calendar year since 2005.<ref name="CRY v ARS PL OptaAnalyst"/>

On 23 December, Arteta confirmed in the pre-match press conference that Saka would be out for a lengthy period after suffering a hamstring injury in the game against Crystal Palace two days prior, and Sterling would also be sidelined for weeks after picking up a knee injury in training three days prior.<ref name="Sterling & Saka suffered injuries SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13278471/bukayo-saka-injury-arsenal-winger-ruled-out-for-many-weeks-with-hamstring-strain-sustained-in-crystal-palace-victory |title=Bukayo Saka injury: Arsenal winger ruled out for 'many weeks' with hamstring strain sustained in Crystal Palace victory |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=23 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=23 Dec 2024}}</ref>

Arsenal ended 2024 with a 1–0 win over newly promoted [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] at home on 27 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2024-Dec-27/arsenal-1-0-ipswich-town-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–0 Ipswich Town |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=27 Dec 2024 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=28 Dec 2024}}</ref> Havertz scored the only goal of the game.<ref name="ARS v IPS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-ipswich-town/report/505977 |title=Arsenal 1–0 Ipswich: Kai Havertz scores only goal as Gunners move above Chelsea into second place |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=27 Dec 2024 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=28 Dec 2024}}</ref> Raya registered his 23rd clean sheet in 50 Premier League appearances for the Gunners, breaking [[David Seaman]]'s record (22) set in 1993 for the most clean sheets kept by a goalkeeper in his first 50 appearances for Arsenal in the division.<ref name="ARS v IPS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4205251 |title=Arsenal go second and cut Liverpool's lead to six points |date=27 Dec 2024 |website=Premier League |access-date=28 Dec 2024}}</ref> This was the first time since 2021 that the Gunners had kept four consecutive home clean sheets in the competition.<ref name="ARS v IPS PL"/> In the post-match presser, Arteta revealed Saka had undergone surgery to repair his hamstring.<ref name="ARS v IPS PL SkySports"/>

===January===
The Gunners started 2025 with a trip to [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on New Year's Day. 17-year-old Ethan Nwaneri was handed his first Premier League start, becoming the youngest player to start for Arsenal in the competition since 2006.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-brentford-1-3-arsenal |title=Report: Brentford 1–3 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=1 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Jan 2025}}</ref> [[Bryan Mbeumo]] gave the hosts an early lead, but a Gabriel Jesus first-half header and second-half strikes from Merino and Martinelli turned the game around.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL AFC"/> This was the first time since February 2023 that Arsenal had won a Premier League away match in which they fell 1–0 behind.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4205602 |title=Arsenal beat Brentford to close gap on leaders Liverpool |date=1 Jan 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=2 Jan 2025}}</ref> Arteta's side reached the halfway point of the league campaign with eleven wins, six draws, two losses and 39 points from 19 games, six points behind leaders Liverpool who had a game in hand.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL"/>

Arteta's side faced 10th-placed Brighton & Hove Albion away on 4 January. Nwaneri netted a 16th-minute opener on his second Premier League start, becoming the first Arsenal player to score more than once in the competition before turning 18 years old.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-04/brighton-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Brighton 1–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Jan 2025}}</ref> But he was forced off with a muscular issue at half-time and was replaced by Martinelli, who made his 200th senior appearance for the Gunners.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC"/> In the 59th minute, Brighton forward João Pedro flicked the ball up in the Arsenal box. Saliba went to head it away, accidentally making contact with Pedro's head in the air.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6033118/2025/01/04/brighton-1-arsenal-1-saliba-penalty-nwaneri/ |title=Brighton 1 Arsenal 1 – A title blow, an unusual penalty call and Nwaneri's cameo |last1=Campbell |first1=Jordan |last2=Raghuraman |first2=Anantaajith |date=4 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=5 Jan 2025}}</ref> However, referee Anthony Taylor awarded the hosts a controversial penalty after a few seconds of reflection, adjudging Saliba to have fouled Pedro, and VAR confirmed the decision.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL EveningStandard">{{cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/joao-pedro-penalty-arsenal-saliba-arsenal-fc-b1202992.html |title=Joao Pedro penalty: Pundits agree over William Saliba headbutt as Arsenal title hopes hit |last=Young |first=Alex |date=5 Jan 2025 |website=[[Evening Standard]] |access-date=5 Jan 2025}}</ref><ref name="BHA v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13284096/joao-pedros-controversial-penalty-for-brighton-vs-arsenal-analysed-what-is-var-doing |title=Joao Pedro's 'controversial' penalty for Brighton vs Arsenal analysed: 'What is VAR doing?' |date=5 Jan 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=5 Jan 2025}}</ref><ref name="BHA v ARS PL GiveMeSport">{{cite web |url=https://www.givemesport.com/footage-william-saliba-var-error-brighton-arsenal/ |title=New Footage Suggests VAR Made Penalty Error During Brighton 1–1 Arsenal |last=Bishop |first=Callum |date=4 Jan 2025 |website=givemesport.com |access-date=5 Jan 2025}}</ref> Pedro then fired home the equaliser from the spot.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC"/> Upon replay, it was clear that Saliba had touched the ball with his head as it deviated away from him in a different direction, before the clash of heads.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL EveningStandard"/><ref name="BHA v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="BHA v ARS PL GiveMeSport"/> The game ended 1–1.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC"/>

Arsenal suffered their first home defeat of the season with a 2–0 loss to Newcastle United in the EFL Cup semi-final first leg on 7 January. They dominated the game and had plenty of chances to score, but failed to convert any.<ref name="ARS v NEW EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-07/arsenal-0-2-newcastle-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0–2 Newcastle United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=7 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jan 2025}}</ref> In fact, they created more than 3.0 [[expected goals]] (xG) from 23 shots throughout the 90 minutes.<ref name="ARS v NEW EFLCup NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6038924/2025/01/07/arsenal-0-newcastle-2-league-cup-semi-final/ |title=Arsenal 0 Newcastle 2 – Eddie Howe's greatest feat yet? What next for Arteta and co? |last1=de Roché |first1=Art |last2=Waugh |first2=Chris |date=7 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=8 Jan 2025}}</ref> Alexander Isak and [[Anthony Gordon (footballer)|Anthony Gordon]] netted either side of the interval for the visitors.<ref name="ARS v NEW EFLCup AFC"/> The result meant that the Magpies departed north London with a two-goal lead heading into the return fixture, which would be on 5 February.<ref name="ARS v NEW EFLCup NYT"/>

On 12 January, the Gunners entered the FA Cup in the third round, facing Manchester United at home. Gabriel Jesus was stretchered off in the first half after an aerial challenge.<ref name="ARS v MUN FACup NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6053551/2025/01/12/arsenal-manchester-united-fa-cup/ |title=Arsenal 1 Man United 1 (Utd win 5–3 on pens): Missed chances, a red, pens and needle in cup thriller |last1=McNicholas |first1=James |last2=Burke |first2=Elias |last3=Critchley |first3=Mark |date=12 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=14 Jan 2025}}</ref> [[Bruno Fernandes]] opened the scoring for the visitors in the second half. Arsenal levelled through Gabriel Magalhães after [[Diogo Dalot]] was sent off for a second bookable offence.<ref name="ARS v MUN FACup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-12/arsenal-1-1-manchester-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–1 Man United (3–5 on penalties) |last=James |first=Josh |date=12 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Jan 2025}}</ref> Ødegaard then saw his penalty saved, and further missed chances – from Havertz and Rice among others – sent the match to extra-time.<ref name="ARS v MUN FACup NYT"/> After a goalless extra 30 minutes, the tie finished 1–1. The Gunners ultimately lost 5–3 on penalties after Havertz's spot-kick was saved.<ref name="ARS v MUN FACup AFC"/> Two days later, Arsenal confirmed that Gabriel Jesus had sustained an injury to the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee and was set for surgery. The club did not give a timeframe for his absence.<ref name="Jesus suffered injury AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/medical-update-gabriel-jesus-injury |title=Medical update on Gabriel Jesus' injury |date=14 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Jan 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal returned to Premier League action on 15 January, hosting 12th-placed Tottenham Hotspur in the second North London derby of the season. [[Son Heung-Min]]'s deflected effort gave the visitors the lead,<ref name="ARS v TOT PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4221361 |title=Arsenal beat Spurs to move four points off the top |date=15 Jan 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Jan 2025}}</ref> but a [[Dominic Solanke]] own goal and a Trossard strike turned the game around before half-time.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-15/arsenal-2-1-tottenham-hotspur-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–1 Tottenham Hotspur |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Jan 2025}}</ref> There were no further goals in the second half and the game ended 2–1.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL"/> The result meant that the Gunners had won three consecutive league matches against their nearest rivals for the first time since 1989.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL AFC"/>

Arteta's side played at home against 7th-placed Aston Villa on 18 January. They took a 2–0 lead courtesy of close-range goals from Martinelli and Havertz either side of half-time.<ref name="ARS v AVL PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-18/arsenal-2-2-aston-villa-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–2 Aston Villa |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 Jan 2025}}</ref> Villa's [[Youri Tielemans]] and Ollie Watkins both struck to level the scores.<ref name="ARS v AVL PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6069638/2025/01/18/arsenal-aston-villa-result-analysis-premier-league/ |title=Arsenal 2 Aston Villa 2: Late VAR anguish as Arteta's side let two-goal lead slip |last1=Campbell |first1=Jordan |last2=Tharme |first2=Liam |date=18 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=19 Jan 2025}}</ref> Arsenal thought they had found a late winner when Merino's shot deflected off Havertz into the net, but it was ruled out for handball after a swift VAR review.<ref name="ARS v AVL PL AFC"/> This was the first time since October 2019 that the Gunners had failed to win a Premier League home game in which they had led by two or more goals.<ref name="ARS v AVL PL AFC"/>

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Champions League home match against Dinamo Zagreb on 22 January<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2042054/ |title=Arsenal vs GNK Dinamo {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=22 Jan 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=23 Jan 2025}}</ref>
}}
Arsenal hosted the previous season's [[2023–24 Croatian Football League|Croatian League]] champions [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] in the Champions League on 22 January. The match saw several records set.<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-22/arsenal-3-0-gnk-dinamo-zagreb-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3–0 Dinamo Zagreb |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=22 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jan 2025}}</ref> Arteta's side took the lead in the second minute when Havertz cushioned a cross into the path of Rice, who volleyed home his first Champions League goal and Arsenal's earliest in the competition since 2014.<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6076179/2025/01/22/arsenal-champions-league-havertz-nwaneri/ |title=Arsenal 3 Dinamo Zagreb 0 – Nwaneri makes welcome return as Arteta's side close in on knockouts |last=Campbell |first=Jordan |date=22 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=23 Jan 2025}}</ref> The Gunners doubled their advantage on 66 minutes as Havertz headed in his 14th goal of the season in all competitions, matching his total from the previous term. It was also the 500th goal Arsenal had scored in all competitions under manager Arteta.<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL AFC"/> In the 74th minute, Trossard came off the bench to replace Havertz, becoming the second Belgian to reach 100 appearances for the club.<ref name="Trossard 100 appearances AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/trossard-completes-100-arsenal-appearances |title=Trossard completes 100 Arsenal appearances |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=23 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jan 2025}}</ref> Ødegaard added a third in stoppage time as he tucked in Trossard's deflected cross. The game also saw academy player [[Nathan Butler-Oyedeji]] come on for the final few minutes to make his senior debut for the Gunners.<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL AFC"/> The 3–0 victory meant that Arsenal had won three consecutive Champions League games by three or more goals for the first time in their history.<ref name="ARS v DZG UCL NYT"/>

The Gunners' eighth match of the month was against 17th-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers on the road on 25 January. Academy players Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri were both named in the starting line-up,<ref name="WOL v ARS PL line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-saliba-returns-face-wolves |title=Team news: Saliba returns to face Wolves |date=25 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> becoming the first two English players aged 18 or under to start a Premier League game together for Arsenal since 1998.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/stats-nwaneri-and-lewis-skelly-end-26-year-wait |title=Stats: Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly end 26 year-wait |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=27 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> In the 43rd minute, Lewis-Skelly tripped [[Matt Doherty (footballer, born 1992)|Matt Doherty]] just outside the Wolves box to stop the hosts' defender breaking from an Arsenal corner.<ref name="WOL v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-25/wolves-0-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Wolves 0–1 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=25 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> However, referee Michael Oliver controversially showed a straight red card to the 18-year-old for "serious foul play", and the decision was quickly checked and cleared by video assistant referee [[Darren England]].<ref name="WOL v ARS PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6080714/2025/01/25/wolves-arsenal-result-report-analysis/ |title=Wolves 0 Arsenal 1: Was Lewis-Skelly's red card harsh? How did Arteta's 10 men play? |last=de Roché |first=Art |date=25 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref><ref name="WOL v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13296511/five-issues-with-myles-lewis-skellys-red-card-in-arsenals-win-at-wolves-premier-league-hits-and-misses |title=Five issues with Myles Lewis-Skelly's red card in Arsenal's win at Wolves – Premier League hits and misses |date=25 Jan 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> In the 63rd minute, Raya produced a full-stretch save to deny [[Matheus Cunha]]'s deflected shot.<ref name="WOL v ARS PL NYT"/> Seven minutes later, Wolves midfielder [[João Gomes (footballer, born 2001)|João Gomes]] received a second yellow for a studs-up challenge on Timber,<ref name="WOL v ARS PL SkySports"/> which left both sides a man down for the remainder of the match. In the 74th minute, substitute Calafiori netted the only goal of the game for the Gunners.<ref name="WOL v ARS PL AFC"/> It was reported on 28 January that Lewis-Skelly would not serve a three-match suspension after Arsenal's appeal against his red card at Wolves was upheld by an [[The Football Association|FA]]'s independent regulatory commission.<ref name="Lewis-Skelly's ban overturned SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13298493/myles-lewis-skelly-arsenal-defenders-red-card-in-wolves-win-overturned-after-successful-appeal |title=Myles Lewis-Skelly: Arsenal defender's red card in Wolves win overturned after successful appeal |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref><ref name="Lewis-Skelly's ban overturned NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6089273/2025/01/28/arsenal-appeal-lewis-skelly-red-card/ |title=Arsenal win appeal against Myles Lewis-Skelly's red card during Wolves victory |last1=McNicholas |first1=James |last2=de Roché |first2=Art |date=28 Jan 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> The written reasons published by the regulatory commission stated that "the Commission members were unanimous in their opinion that the Referee had made an obvious error in sending off MLS for the challenge that he had made."<ref name="written reasons FA PDF">{{cite web |url=https://www.thefa.com/-/media/files/thefaportal/governance-docs/discipline-cases/2025/claim-of-wrongful-dismissal-and-clearly-excessive---myles-lewis-skelly---28-january-2025.ashx |title=Claim of Wrongful Dismissal and Clearly Excessive – Myles Lewis-Skelly – 28 January 2025 – Written Reasons |date=28 Jan 2025 |website=The Football Association |format=PDF |access-date=1 Feb 2025 |archive-date=1 Feb 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250201154230/https://www.thefa.com/-/media/files/thefaportal/governance-docs/discipline-cases/2025/claim-of-wrongful-dismissal-and-clearly-excessive---myles-lewis-skelly---28-january-2025.ashx |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="written reasons SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13300327/myles-lewis-skelly-red-card-fa-reveals-why-arsenal-defenders-sending-off-was-overturned-after-appeal |title=Myles Lewis-Skelly red card: FA reveals why Arsenal defender's sending off was overturned after appeal |date=31 Jan 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> "MLS had stepped across his opponent and tripped him up, possibly deliberately, but in doing so he had obviously not endangered the safety of his opponent or used excessive force or brutality, nor had he 'lunged' in at his opponent."<ref name="written reasons FA PDF"/><ref name="written reasons SkySports"/>

Arsenal made the trip to Spain on 29 January for the final Champions League league-phase game against La Liga side [[Girona FC|Girona]].<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2042077/ |title=Girona vs Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> Arteta handed a belated debut to summer loan signing Neto, who at 35 years and 194 days became Arsenal's oldest debutant since 1915;<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL Talksport">{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/2860875/arsenal-neto-debut-record-champions-league/ |title=Neto instantly achieves feat only bettered 110 years ago during Arsenal clash – but makes huge blunder on debut |last=Lambourne |first=Jake |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=[[Talksport]] |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> while Gabriel Magalhães made his 200th senior appearance for the Gunners.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL line-up AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-neto-makes-arsenal-debut-girona |title=Team news: Neto makes Arsenal debut at Girona |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> [[Arnaut Danjuma]] opened the scoring for the hosts in the 28th minute.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL Talksport"/> Jorginho equalised with a spot-kick on 38 minutes.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Jan-29/girona-fc-1-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Girona 1–2 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> Nwaneri put Arsenal ahead with a curling effort four minutes later, becoming the second-youngest Englishman to score a Champions League goal.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/girona-vs-arsenal/report/521733 |title=Girona 1–2 Arsenal: Ethan Nwaneri scores on first Champions League start as Gunners seal last-16 spot |date=29 Jan 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Feb 2025}}</ref> Girona thought they had drawn level through [[Cristhian Stuani]] in the 77th minute, only for VAR to intervene for offside in the build-up.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL AFC"/> In stoppage time Sterling saw his penalty saved by Girona goalkeeper.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL SkySports"/> The 2–1 victory meant that the Gunners had secured consecutive away wins in the competition for the first time since December 2016.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL AFC"/> Arteta's side finished third in the Champions League league phase and bypassed February's play-off round to go straight to the last 16.<ref name="GIR v ARS UCL SkySports"/>

====First-team transfers (winter transfer window)====
The Premier League [[List of English football transfers winter 2024–25|winter transfer window]] ran from 1 January to 3 February 2025.<ref name="Transfer windows PL"/>

On 9 January, Arsenal announced that Brazilian forward [[Marquinhos (footballer, born 2003)|Marquinhos]] had joined [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] side [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] on loan until December 2025.<ref name="Marquinhos loaned out AFC"/>

The club did not sign any player in the winter transfer window. After the transfer window closed, there were twenty-two players in the first-team squad: two goalkeepers, nine defenders, five midfielders, and six forwards. Six other first-team players were out on loan.<ref name="first-team squad (Feb) AFC"/>

===February===
{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Premier League home match against Manchester City on 2 February<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/116057 |title=Arsenal v Man City, 2024/25 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=2 Feb 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=3 Feb 2025}}</ref>
}}
The Gunners played at home against 4th-placed Manchester City on 2 February. Ødegaard put Arsenal ahead in the 2nd minute with a tap-in following a Havertz pass.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6097469/2025/02/02/arsenal-manchester-city-premier-league-lewis-skelly-nwaneri-haaland/ |title=Arsenal 5 Manchester City 1: Lewis-Skelly's moment, Nwaneri's magic and so many City errors |last1=McNicholas |first1=James |last2=Lee |first2=Sam |last3=Harris |first3=Thom |date=2 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=3 Feb 2025}}</ref> Raya made two vital saves to keep out [[Joško Gvardiol]]'s close-range header and [[Savinho]]'s low strike in the first half.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4237257 |title=Arsenal THRASH Man City to go six points behind leaders Liverpool |date=2 Feb 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=3 Feb 2025}}</ref> City drew level on 55 minutes through Erling Haaland, but the hosts retook the lead just a minute later through Partey's deflected strike from outside the box.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL"/> In the 62nd minute, 18-year-old Lewis-Skelly took a pass from Rice and curled a right-footed shot beyond visiting goalkeeper [[Stefan Ortega]] for his first senior goal.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Feb-02/arsenal-5-1-manchester-city-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 5–1 Manchester City |last=James |first=Josh |date=2 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 Feb 2025}}</ref> Havertz then made it four after a swift counter-attack on 76 minutes.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL AFC"/> In stoppage time Rice launched a long pass from the left flank to 17-year-old Nwaneri, who cut inside from the right and fired a long-range curling effort around Ortega into the bottom corner.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL NYT"/> This was the first time Arsenal had had two teenagers scoring for the club in the same league game since 1986.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL AFC 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/records-broken-and-great-stats-our-city-win |title=Records broken and great stats from our City win |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=3 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 Feb 2025}}</ref> The 5–1 victory was the Gunners' biggest win over Manchester City since 2003, and their biggest-ever win over the reigning Premier League champions in their history.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL AFC 2"/> Arteta became the third manager to go five games unbeaten in all competitions against City boss [[Pep Guardiola]], after [[Thomas Tuchel]] and [[Jürgen Klopp]].<ref name="ARS v MCI PL"/> The result saw Arsenal extend their unbeaten run to 14 consecutive Premier League games for the first time under Arteta.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL"/>

Arsenal travelled to Newcastle United for the second leg of their EFL Cup semi-final on 5 February. Goals from [[Jacob Murphy]] and Anthony Gordon either side of half-time knocked the Gunners out of the competition with an aggregate scoreline of 4–0.<ref name="NEW v ARS EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Feb-05/newcastle-united-2-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Newcastle United 2–0 Arsenal (4–0 agg) |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=5 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=6 Feb 2025}}</ref> The game also saw Martinelli limp off the pitch with a hamstring injury on 37 minutes.<ref name="NEW v ARS EFLCup NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6109344/2025/02/05/newcastle-2-arsenal-0-agg-4-0-howe-isak-gordon-wembley/ |title=Newcastle 2 Arsenal 0 (agg: 4–0) – Howe's system shock, Isak toys with Saliba, Wembley awaits |last1=Waugh |first1=Chris |last2=Campbell |first2=Jordan |last3=Raghuraman |first3=Anantaajith |date=5 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=6 Feb 2025}}</ref> It was later reported that he would be sidelined for more than a month.<ref name="Martinelli suffered injury NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6122150/2025/02/07/arsenal-martinelli-hamstring-injury-update/ |title=Arsenal's Gabriel Martinelli faces more than a month on sidelines with hamstring injury |last=Ornstein |first=David |date=7 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=7 Feb 2025}}</ref>

On 6 February, the squad travelled to Dubai, United Arab Emirates for a warm-weather training camp.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/squad-head-dubai-warm-weather-training |title=Squad head to Dubai for warm weather training |last=Wright |first=Stephen |date=6 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Feb 2025}}</ref> They flew back to England on 11 February.

Ten days after the winter transfer window closed, the club confirmed on 13 February that Havertz had sustained a hamstring injury during their training camp in Dubai and was set for surgery.<ref name="Havertz suffered injury AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/injury-update-kai-havertz |title=Injury update: Kai Havertz |date=13 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Feb 2025}}</ref><ref name="Havertz suffered injury NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6131108/2025/02/13/havertz-injury-surgery-arsenal/ |title=Arsenal's Kai Havertz to undergo surgery on torn hamstring injury, will miss rest of 2024–25 |last1=Rampling |first1=Ali |last2=de Roché |first2=Art |date=13 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=14 Feb 2025}}</ref> With Gabriel Jesus, Martinelli and Saka already sidelined through injury, Havertz's absence left Arteta with just two first-team forwards to choose from up front in Sterling and Trossard.<ref name="Havertz suffered injury NYT"/>

The Gunners returned to action with a game against 17th-placed Leicester City away on 15 February. With the score standing at 0–0 in the 69th minute, Arteta brought on midfielder Merino as a makeshift striker.<ref name="LEI v ARS PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6126139/2025/02/15/leicester-city-arsenal-premier-league/ |title=Leicester City 0 Arsenal 2: Is Merino the answer? Nwaneri stands out; Lewis-Skelly's composure |last=Campbell |first=Jordan |date=15 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=16 Feb 2025}}</ref> The Spaniard broke the deadlock on 81 minutes when he headed home a cross from Nwaneri, who became the youngest Arsenal player to assist a Premier League goal since 2008.<ref name="LEI v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4243572 |title=Merino's brace as Arsenal's No 9 cuts gap at the top to four points |date=15 Feb 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Feb 2025}}</ref> Six minutes later, Merino netted his second of the afternoon at the back post to seal the win,<ref name="LEI v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Feb-15/leicester-city-0-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Leicester City 0–2 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=15 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Feb 2025}}</ref> becoming the first Arsenal player to score twice as a substitute in a Premier League away game since 2018.<ref name="LEI v ARS PL"/>

On 19 February, the club confirmed that Tomiyasu had undergone surgery to his right knee and would be out until the end of 2025.<ref name="Tomiyasu underwent surgery AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/medical-update-takehiro-tomiyasu |title=Medical update: Takehiro Tomiyasu |date=19 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=20 Feb 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal suffered their first home defeat of the Premier League season with a 1–0 loss to 16th-placed West Ham United on 22 February. [[Jarrod Bowen]] scored the decisive goal on 44 minutes following a swift counter-attack, helping his side secure back-to-back wins at Emirates Stadium.<ref name="ARS v WHU PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Feb-22/arsenal-0-1-west-ham-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0–1 West Ham United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=22 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Feb 2025}}</ref> In the 73rd minute, substitute Lewis-Skelly had a yellow card upgraded to a red for denying a goalscoring opportunity on the halfway line following a VAR check.<ref name="ARS v WHU PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6151448/2025/02/22/arsenal-west-ham-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 0 West Ham 1: Unbeaten run over, Lewis-Skelly's red card and the Merino experiment |last=de Roché |first=Art |date=22 Feb 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=23 Feb 2025}}</ref> The result ended the Gunners' 15-game unbeaten run in the Premier League.<ref name="ARS v WHU PL AFC"/>

The Gunners faced 3rd-placed Nottingham Forest away on 26 February. Neither side could find the breakthrough and the match finished 0–0.<ref name="NFO v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Feb-26/nottingham-forest-0-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Nottingham Forest 0–0 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=26 Feb 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Mar 2025}}</ref> It was the first time since May 2023 that Arsenal had failed to score in back-to-back Premier League games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4251396 |title=Arsenal drop more points in title race with draw at Forest |date=26 Feb 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=1 Mar 2025}}</ref>

===March===
{{football squad on pitch|align=right|flag_template=flagg2
| GK_nat = ESP | GK = Raya
| RB_nat = NED | RB = Timber

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Champions League away match against PSV Eindhoven on 4 March<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2044819--psv-vs-arsenal/ |title=PSV vs Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=4 Mar 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=5 Mar 2025}}</ref>
}}
On 4 March, Arteta's men travelled to the Netherlands to face the previous season's [[2023–24 Eredivisie|Eredivisie]] champions [[PSV Eindhoven]] in the Champions League [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|last-16 first leg]].<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Mar-04/psv-eindhoven-1-7-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: PSV Eindhoven 1–7 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=4 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Mar 2025}}</ref> The game saw Arsenal break numerous club and competition records.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL records AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gunners-smash-champions-league-record-against-psv |title=Gunners smash Champions League record against PSV |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Mar 2025}}</ref><ref name="PSV v ARS UCL PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4261577 |title=What we learned from Tuesday's Champions League matches |last=Hancock |first=Tom |date=5 Mar 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Mar 2025}}</ref><ref name="PSV v ARS UCL TheAnalyst">{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2025/03/psv-1-7-arsenal-stats-opta-champions-league |title=PSV 1–7 Arsenal Stats: Gunners Run Riot in Eindhoven with Seven-Goal Victory |last=Furniss |first=Matt |date=4 Mar 2025 |website=The Analyst |access-date=5 Mar 2025}}</ref> Through Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri the Gunners started a Champions League knockout match with two teenagers for the first time since March 2007 versus PSV,<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL records AFC"/> and Nwaneri became the second-youngest Arsenal player to make a Champions League knockout appearance.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL PL"/> Dutchman Timber opened the scoring for the visitors in the 18th minute.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL AFC"/> Nwaneri doubled the lead on 21 minutes, becoming the third-youngest player to net a knockout stage goal in the competition.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/> Makeshift striker Merino put the Gunners 3–0 up in the 31st minute. [[Noa Lang]] pulled one back for the hosts from the spot just before half-time.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL AFC"/> Courtesy of quickfire strikes from Ødegaard and Trossard, Arsenal reached the five-goal mark on 48 minutes, the earliest by any away side ever in a Champions League knockout game.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL PL"/> Ødegaard added his second and the Gunners' sixth in the 73rd minute. Substitute Calafiori completed the rout on 85 minutes.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL AFC"/> This was the first time Arsenal had hit seven in the Champions League since October 2007 versus [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]].<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL records AFC"/> The 7–1 triumph over PSV was Arsenal's first Champions League knockout win in a decade,<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL PL"/> and their first win on Dutch soil for 17 years.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL records AFC"/> In fact, it was the Gunners' biggest away win in the competition,<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL PL"/> while they became the first team in Champions League history to score seven or more goals away from home in a knockout game.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/> Arsenal also became the first side to have six different scorers (excluding own goals) in an away knockout match in the competition.<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/> The result meant that they had won five consecutive Champions League games in a single edition of the competition for the first time since [[2005–06 Arsenal F.C. season|2005–06]].<ref name="PSV v ARS UCL records AFC"/>

Arsenal faced 14th-placed Manchester United away on 9 March. They went behind on the stroke of half-time when Bruno Fernandes curled a 25-yard free-kick past a badly positioned Raya in goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6180024/2025/03/09/manchester-united-arsenal-analysis/ |title=Man United 1 Arsenal 1: Rice rescue act, Fernandes' brilliance and fan protests |last1=Whitwell |first1=Laurie |last2=Campbell |first2=Jordan |last3=O'Neill |first3=Conor |date=9 Mar 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=10 Mar 2025}}</ref> It was later revealed by broadcaster Sky Sports that referee Anthony Taylor marched the Arsenal defensive line 11.2 yards back, further than the minimum 10 yards required in the [[International Football Association Board|IFAB]] [[Laws of the Game (association football)|Laws of the Game]], before Fernandes played the ball over the Arsenal wall inside the near post.<ref name="MUN v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/man-utd-vs-arsenal/report/506082 |title=Man Utd 1–1 Arsenal: Declan Rice rescues a dramatic draw for Gunners after Bruno Fernandes' controversial free-kick |last=Smith |first=Peter |date=9 Mar 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=10 Mar 2025}}</ref> In the second half, Rice scored an equaliser and then made a last-ditch tackle to deny Rasmus Højlund,<ref name="MUN v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Mar-09/manchester-united-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Man Utd 1–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=9 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Mar 2025}}</ref> before Raya's double save in the final seconds – which would later win March 2025's [[Premier League Save of the Month]] award – kept the match level.<ref name="MUN v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="Raya won March's PL SOTM"/> The 1–1 draw marked Arteta's 200th Premier League match in charge. The Spaniard had won 118 times in his first 200 top-flight games as Gunners boss, eight more wins than [[Arsène Wenger]] had achieved at the same milestone (110).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2025/03/mikel-arteta-200-premier-league-games-arsenal-man-utd |title=Mikel Arteta – 200 Premier League Games, 118 Wins: Where Does He Rank Among the Greats? |last=Hopkins |first=Oliver |date=9 Mar 2025 |website=The Analyst |access-date=10 Mar 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal hosted PSV Eindhoven in the second leg of the Champions League round of 16 on 12 March. With his side leading 7–1 from the first leg, Arteta took the opportunity to name a much-changed XI which included Zinchenko in midfield and Tierney on the left wing.<ref name="ARS v PSV UCL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-psv/report/528713 |title=Arsenal 2–2 PSV Eindhoven (9–3 agg): Raheem Sterling impresses as Gunners ease into Champions League last eight |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=12 Mar 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=14 Mar 2025}}</ref> Goals from Zinchenko and Rice put the Gunners ahead on two occasions but the visitors levelled up twice, and the game ended 2–2.<ref name="ARS v PSV UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Mar-12/arsenal-2-2-psv-eindhoven-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–2 PSV Eindhoven |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=12 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Mar 2025}}</ref> After completing a 9–3 aggregate win over PSV, Arsenal booked their place in the Champions League quarter-finals.<ref name="ARS v PSV UCL SkySports"/> This was the first time since 2010 that they had clinched successive last-eight appearances in the competition.<ref name="ARS v PSV UCL AFC"/>

Ahead of the last international break of the season, the Gunners hosted 4th-placed Chelsea on 16 March. Merino netted the only goal of the game with a header from Ødegaard's corner,<ref name="ARS v CHE PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-chelsea/report/506087 |title=Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea: Mikel Merino winner from another Gunners set-piece beats Blues in feisty Premier League derby |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=16 Mar 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=17 Mar 2025}}</ref> helping his side end a three-game winless run in the Premier League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Mar-16/arsenal-1-0-chelsea-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea |last=James |first=Josh |date=16 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=17 Mar 2025}}</ref>

Fourteen Arsenal players (excluding loaned out players) were named in their respective countries' senior squads for international fixtures in March: Trossard (Belgium), Gabriel Magalhães (Brazil), Lewis-Skelly and Rice (England), Saliba (France), Partey (Ghana), Calafiori (Italy), Timber (Netherlands), Ødegaard (as Norway's captain), Kiwior (Poland), Tierney (Scotland), Merino and Raya (Spain), and Zinchenko (Ukraine).<ref name="Intl call-ups Mar 2025 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/14-gunners-selected-international-duty |title=14 Gunners selected for international duty |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=18 Mar 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 Mar 2025}}</ref> This was the first time for Lewis-Skelly to be called up to the England senior team.<ref name="England call-ups Mar 2025">{{cite web |url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2025/Mar/14/england-mens-senior-squad-named-by-thomas-tuchel-for-albania-latvia-games-20251403 |title=Thomas Tuchel has named his first England squad |last=Veevers |first=Nicholas |date=14 Mar 2025 |website=englandfootball.com |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=14 Mar 2025}}</ref> Aged 18 years and 176 days, he became England's youngest debutant scorer during a [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2026 World Cup qualifier]] victory over Albania on 21 March.<ref name="Lewis-Skelly ENG debut NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6222216/2025/03/21/myles-lewis-skelly-england-debut/ |title=Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly 'lost for words' after record-breaking England debut |last=Rampling |first=Ali |date=21 Mar 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=22 Mar 2025}}</ref>

===April===
Arteta's side played at home against 8th-placed Fulham on 1 April. They lost Gabriel Magalhães to injury early on but went ahead through makeshift striker Merino.<ref name="ARS v FUL PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-01/arsenal-2-1-fulham-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–1 Fulham |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Apr 2025}}</ref> This was the Spaniard's sixth Premier League goal for the Gunners this season, his most in a single campaign in his league career.<ref name="ARS v FUL PL AFC"/> Second-half substitute Saka marked his return from a three-month injury lay-off by heading in an acrobatic flick from Martinelli at the back post.<ref name="ARS v FUL PL AFC"/> [[Rodrigo Muniz (Brazilian footballer)|Rodrigo Muniz]] scored a late consolation goal for Fulham.<ref name="ARS v FUL PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6243964/2025/04/01/arsenal-fulham-result-analysis/ |title=Arsenal 2 Fulham 1: Saka's dream return, Gabriel injury concern and Merino scores again |last=McNicholas |first=James |date=1 Apr 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=2 Apr 2025}}</ref> Two days later, Arsenal confirmed that Gabriel Magalhães had sustained a hamstring injury which would require surgery and rule him out of the rest of the season.<ref name="Magalhães suffered injury AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/injury-update-gabriel-magalhaes |title=Injury update: Gabriel Magalhaes |date=3 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=4 Apr 2025}}</ref>

The Gunners headed to [[Goodison Park]] for the 113th and final time to take on 15th-placed Everton on 5 April.<ref name="EVE v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-05/everton-1-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Everton 1–1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=5 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=6 Apr 2025}}</ref> Trossard opened the scoring for the visitors from a counter-attack on 34 minutes.<ref name="EVE v ARS PL AFC"/> Everton were awarded a controversial penalty by referee [[Darren England]] early in the second half when Lewis-Skelly was adjudged to have fouled [[Jack Harrison (footballer, born 1996)|Jack Harrison]],<ref name="EVE v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/everton-vs-arsenal/report/506110 |title=Everton 1–1 Arsenal: Gunners held as Iliman Ndiaye's 'soft' penalty clinches draw for Toffees |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=5 Apr 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=6 Apr 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/videos/cg4155d1z91o |title=Match of the Day: Why Everton penalty was a 'really bad decision' |date=5 Apr 2025 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=6 Apr 2025}}</ref> and [[Iliman Ndiaye]] then sent Raya the wrong way from 12 yards.<ref name="EVE v ARS PL SkySports"/> The game ended 1–1.<ref name="EVE v ARS PL AFC"/>

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Champions League home match against Real Madrid on 8 April<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2044849/ |title=Arsenal vs Real Madrid {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=8 Apr 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref>
}}
Arsenal hosted 15-time and reigning European champions [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the Champions League quarter-final first leg on 8 April.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-08/arsenal-3-0-real-madrid-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3–0 Real Madrid |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=8 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref> Lewis-Skelly was named in the starting line-up, becoming the second youngest English player to start a Champions League quarter-final.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0298-1d798677eb22-40b84d719d26-1000--arsenal-3-0-real-madrid-sublime-declan-rice-free-kicks-inspi/ |title=Arsenal 3–0 Real Madrid: Sublime Declan Rice free-kicks inspire famous Gunners victory |date=8 Apr 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref> After a goalless first half in which Raya saved a one-on-one chance from [[Kylian Mbappé]], Rice broke the deadlock on 58 minutes when he curled a strike around the Real Madrid wall and just inside visiting goalkeeper [[Thibaut Courtois]]' left-hand post.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA 2"/> This was the first direct [[Free kick (association football)|free-kick]] goal of his senior career,<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6261133/2025/04/08/arsenal-3-real-madrid-0-declan-rice-free-kicks/ |title=Arsenal 3 Real Madrid 0 – Breaking down Declan Rice's two incredible free kicks |last1=Campbell |first1=Jordan |last2=Lang |first2=Jack |last3=Carey |first3=Mark |date=8 Apr 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref> making him the fourth Arsenal player to score from a direct free-kick in the Champions League.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL AFC"/> Rice netted his second of the night with another free-kick in the 70th minute, as he bent an effort past the outstretched Courtois and into the top right corner.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA 2"/><ref name="ARS v RMA UCL NYT"/> In doing so, he became the fifth player in Champions League history to score two direct free-kick goals in the same game, and the first to score two in a Champions League knockout match.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL NYT"/> Merino added a third five minutes later, sweeping in a first-time curling strike into the bottom left corner from a Lewis-Skelly pass.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA 2"/> In stoppage time, Real Madrid midfielder [[Eduardo Camavinga]] was sent off after receiving a second yellow card.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL NYT"/> The win gave Arteta's side a three-goal advantage heading to the second leg in Madrid the next week.<ref name="ARS v RMA UCL UEFA 2"/> The victory also meant that England had secured a top-two spot in [[UEFA]]'s [[UEFA coefficient#Men's association coefficient|association club coefficient]] rankings, which would bring a fifth Champions League spot for the Premier League in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4236670 |title=Premier League claims fifth UEFA Champions League spot |date=8 Apr 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref>

It was reported on 9 April that Arteta's backroom staff – including assistant coaches [[Albert Stuivenberg]], [[Carlos Cuesta (football manager)|Carlos Cuesta]], [[Nicolas Jover]], [[Miguel Molina (footballer)|Miguel Molina]] and goalkeeping coach [[Iñaki Caña]] – had all penned new contracts with the club, which would keep them at Emirates Stadium until 2027.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-fc-new-contracts-arteta-jover-b1221627.html |title=Arsenal agree five new contracts as Mikel Arteta backroom staff sign extensions |last=Collings |first=Simon |date=9 Apr 2025 |website=Evening Standard |access-date=9 Apr 2025}}</ref>

The Gunners played at home against 12th-placed Brentford on 12 April. After a scoreless first half that saw Tierney had a goal ruled out by the new [[semi-automated offside technology]],<ref name="ARS v BRE PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6266580/2025/04/12/arsenal-brentford-analysis-premier-league/ |title=Arsenal 1 Brentford 1 – Partey scores but Arteta's side held to a fourth league draw in six |last1=de Roché |first1=Art |last2=Tharme |first2=Liam |date=12 Apr 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=14 Apr 2025}}</ref> Arteta's side took the lead with a counter-attacking goal finished off by Partey.<ref name="ARS v BRE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-12/arsenal-1-1-brentford-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–1 Brentford |last=James |first=Josh |date=12 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Apr 2025}}</ref> But the visitors levelled through [[Yoane Wissa]] later.<ref name="ARS v BRE PL NYT"/> Arsenal failed to find a winner, and they were forced to finish the game with ten men as Jorginho hobbled off injured after they had used all their five substitutions.<ref name="ARS v BRE PL AFC"/>

On 16 April, Arteta's men travelled to Real Madrid for the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2044855/ |title=Real Madrid vs Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Champions League 2024/25 |date=16 Apr 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=17 Apr 2025}}</ref> In the 11th minute Arsenal were awarded a penalty, after the VAR spotted Real defender [[Raúl Asencio (footballer, born 2003)|Raúl Asencio]] had hauled down Merino from a corner.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-16/real-madrid-1-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Real Madrid 1–2 Arsenal (1–5 agg) |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=16 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=17 Apr 2025}}</ref> But Saka's attempted [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka]] was clawed away by goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6278171/2025/04/16/real-madrid-arsenal-champions-league-analysis-talking-points/ |title=Real Madrid 1 Arsenal 2 (1–5 agg) – Exceptional Arsenal, Saka strikes back and Madrid's 42 crosses |last1=de Roché |first1=Art |last2=James |first2=Stuart |last3=Carey |first3=Mark |date=16 Apr 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=17 Apr 2025}}</ref> In the 23rd minute the hosts were given a spot kick of their own, after Rice was adjudged to have pulled down Kylian Mbappé in the box.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL AFC"/> The decision was overturned following another VAR intervention.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL NYT"/> Saka redeemed himself on 65 minutes as he broke the offside trap to collect Merino's through ball and chipped over Courtois.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL AFC"/> Real hit back just two minutes later when a mistake from Saliba gifted [[Vinícius Júnior]] with an open goal to score.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL NYT"/> In stoppage time, Merino sent Martinelli through on goal from the halfway line, and the Brazilian slotted the ball past Courtois to seal a 2–1 win for Arsenal.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL AFC"/> The result meant that Arteta's side completed a 5–1 aggregate triumph over Real Madrid,<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL NYT"/> who had still yet to beat the Gunners in four European encounters.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL AFC"/> This was the second time Arsenal had eliminated the reigning Champions League champions, after previously doing so versus [[AC Milan]] in [[2007–08 Arsenal F.C. season|2007–08]].<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL TheAnalyst">{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2025/04/real-madrid-vs-arsenal-stats-opta-champions-league |title=Real Madrid 1–2 Arsenal Stats (1–5 agg): Arsenal Sleek, Madrid Meek as Gunners Seal Memorable Victory Over European Giants |last=Furniss |first=Matt |date=16 Apr 2025 |website=The Analyst |access-date=17 Apr 2025}}</ref> The result also meant that the Gunners qualified the Champions League semi-finals for the third time in their history, after 2005–06 and 2008–09;<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/> and Arteta became the 10th different Spanish manager to reach a Champions League semi-final.<ref name="RMA v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/>

Arsenal faced 18th-placed Ipswich Town away on 20 April. Trossard gave them an early lead with their 100th goal of the campaign in all competitions.<ref name="IPS v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-20/ipswich-town-0-4-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Ipswich Town 0–4 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=20 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=21 Apr 2025}}</ref> In the 28th minute, Saka raced down the right and sent the ball across the Ipswich box, with Merino backheeling into the path of Martinelli to tap in his 50th goal for the Gunners.<ref name="IPS v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/ipswich-vs-arsenal/report/506132 |title=Ipswich 0–4 Arsenal: Leandro Trossard scores twice and Bukayo Saka shines as Gunners deny Liverpool Premier League title win on Sunday |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=20 Apr 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=21 Apr 2025}}</ref><ref name="IPS v ARS PL AFC"/> The hosts were reduced to 10 men on 32 minutes as left-back [[Leif Davis]] was shown a straight red card for raking his studs down Saka's right [[Achilles tendon]].<ref name="IPS v ARS PL SkySports"/> In the second half, Trossard added a third to complete a brace.<ref name="IPS v ARS PL AFC"/> Substitute Nwaneri netted the fourth goal via a double deflection.<ref name="IPS v ARS PL SkySports"/> The 4–0 win meant that Arsenal were unbeaten in their last 12 Premier League away matches, their longest run within a single season since 2008–09.<ref name="IPS v ARS PL AFC"/>

Arteta's side played at home against 12th-placed Crystal Palace on 23 April. The Gunners took the lead through Kiwior's header. [[Eberechi Eze]] levelled for the visitors with a volley from a corner.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6301450/2025/04/23/arsenal-2-crystal-palace-2-kiwior-saliba-trossard/ |title=Arsenal 2 Crystal Palace 2 – Towering Kiwior, sloppy Saliba, Trossard's confidence boost |last=Campbell |first=Jordan |date=23 Apr 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=24 Apr 2025}}</ref> Trossard restored Arsenal's advantage before the break. The hosts thought they had a third goal through Martinelli in the second half, but it was ruled out after a VAR review.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-23/arsenal-2-2-crystal-palace-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2–2 Crystal Palace |last=James |first=Josh |date=23 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=24 Apr 2025}}</ref> On the other end, Jean-Philippe Mateta capitalised on Saliba's poor pass and scored a late equaliser for the Eagles.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL NYT"/> It was Arsenal's ninth draw in a Premier League game where they had been leading in this season.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL AFC"/>

The Gunners hosted the newly minted French champions Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-final first leg on 29 April.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-SF AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Apr-29/arsenal-0-1-psg-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0–1 PSG |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=29 Apr 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Apr 2025}}</ref> The French side dominated the opening stages and went ahead through [[Ousmane Dembélé]] in the 4th minute.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-SF UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0298-1da3c1fb8af8-2d1affb78bbd-1000--arsenal-0-1-paris-visitors-earn-impressive-away-win-thanks/ |title=Arsenal 0–1 Paris: Visitors earn impressive away win thanks to early Ousmane Dembélé goal |date=29 Apr 2025 |website=UEFA |access-date=30 Apr 2025}}</ref> Merino headed in Rice's free-kick on 47 minutes, but the Spaniard was adjudged to have been offside following a lengthy VAR check.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-SF AFC"/> Nwaneri came off the bench to replace Ødegaard in the 90th minute, becoming the youngest English player to make a Champions League semi-final appearance.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-SF UEFA"/> The 1–0 defeat saw Arsenal's 17 European game unbeaten run at home come to an end.<ref name="ARS v PSG UCL-SF UEFA"/>

===May===
Arsenal suffered their second home defeat of the Premier League campaign with a 2–1 loss to 10th-placed Bournemouth on 3 May. Rice marked his 100th appearance for the Gunners with the opener in the 34th minute.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-03/arsenal-1-2-bournemouth-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–2 Bournemouth |last=James |first=Josh |date=3 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=4 May 2025}}</ref> [[Dean Huijsen]]'s header from a long throw brought Bournemouth level on 67 minutes.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL AFC"/> Evanilson completed the turn around with a 75th-minute goal at the far post from a corner, after a lengthy VAR review determined that there was no conclusive evidence he had handled the ball.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL ESPN">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704619 |title=Bournemouth fight back to seal first-ever win at Arsenal |date=3 May 2025 |website=ESPN |access-date=4 May 2025}}</ref> The result meant that Arsenal had dropped 21 points from winning positions in the Premier League this season.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL ESPN"/>

On 7 May, Arteta's side travelled to Paris Saint-Germain for the second leg of their Champions League semi-final. Despite going close early on through Rice, Martinelli and Ødegaard, the Gunners fell behind on 27 minutes when [[Fabián Ruiz]]'s shot deflected off Saliba into the net.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6336860/2025/05/07/psg-2-arsenal-1-champions-league-donnarumma-arteta/ |title=PSG 2 Arsenal 1 (agg: 3–1): Decisive Donnarumma, worthy finalists, Arteta's set-piece problem |last1=Lang |first1=Jack |last2=Campbell |first2=Jordan |last3=Carey |first3=Mark |date=7 May 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref> The hosts were awarded a spot kick following a VAR check for a handball by Lewis-Skelly, but Raya dived to his left to save [[Vitinha (footballer, born February 2000)|Vitinha]]'s 69th-minute penalty.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-07/paris-saint-germain-fc-2-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Paris Saint-Germain 2–1 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=7 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref> In the 72nd minute [[Achraf Hakimi]] curled home to double PSG's lead.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL NYT"/> Saka pulled a goal back on 76 minutes, but then blew a golden chance to draw level by shooting over an open goal from six yards shortly after.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL NYT"/> Arsenal had many opportunities to score during the game, but only managed to find the net once. In fact, they created more than 3.0 expected goals (xG) from 19 shots throughout the 90 minutes.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL TheAnalyst">{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2025/05/psg-vs-arsenal-stats-champions-league-semi-final-opta |title=PSG 2–1 Arsenal Stats (3–1 agg): Parisians Best Gunners to Reach Champions League Final |last=Segar |first=David |date=7 May 2025 |website=The Analyst |access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref> The 2–1 defeat meant that the Gunners were eliminated from the Champions League at the semi-final stage with an aggregate scoreline of 3–1.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL AFC"/> This was the fourth time since 2021 that Arsenal had failed to progress past major cup semi-finals, after [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|2020–21 Europa League]], [[2021–22 EFL Cup]] and 2024–25 EFL Cup; and was their longest-ever run of exits at this stage.<ref name="PSG v ARS UCL TheAnalyst"/>

The Gunners headed to Liverpool to take on the newly crowned Premier League champions on 11 May. They gave Liverpool a guard of honour before kick-off.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4304651 |title=Arsenal fight back from two goals down to draw against Liverpool |date=11 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref> The hosts went 2–0 up in the first half through two quickfire goals from [[Cody Gakpo]] and [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]].<ref name="LIV v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-11/liverpool-2-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Liverpool 2–2 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=11 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref> Arteta's side battled back after the break thanks to headers from Martinelli and Merino, who was sent off for a second bookable offence later.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL AFC"/> The game ended 2–2.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL"/> This was the first time since March 2021 that Arsenal had avoided defeat after being at least two goals down at half-time in a Premier League match.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL"/>

| caption = Starting XI (4–3–3) for Premier League home match against Newcastle United on 18 May<ref name="ARS v NEW PL 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/116187 |title=Arsenal v Newcastle, 2024/25 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=18 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=19 May 2025}}</ref>
}}
In their final home game of the season, Arteta's side faced 3rd-placed Newcastle United on 18 May.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-18/arsenal-1-0-newcastle-united-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1–0 Newcastle United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=18 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 May 2025}}</ref> Goalkeeper Raya produced a man of the match display with several crucial saves, helping Arsenal win 1–0 and recording his 13th clean sheet of the Premier League campaign.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL 2"/> Rice struck the winner on 55 minutes with a first-time finish after being picked out by Ødegaard.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL AFC"/> The game also saw the return from injury of Havertz, who came on as a replacement for Saka in the 76th minute.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4309268 |title=Rice fires Arsenal into Champions League with win over Newcastle |date=18 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=19 May 2025}}</ref> The result ended the Gunners' five-match winless run in all competitions, and ensured they qualified for next season's Champions League.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL"/>

On 21 May, the club confirmed that Timber had undergone ankle surgery the day prior while Saliba had injured a hamstring against Newcastle. They both would be out for a few weeks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/injury-update-william-saliba-and-jurrien-timber |title=Injury update on William Saliba and Jurrien Timber |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=21 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 May 2025}}</ref>

Arsenal's 58th and final game of the campaign was against 20th-placed Southampton on the road on 25 May. Arteta watched the game from the stands as he served a one-match touchline ban.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-May-25/southampton-1-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Southampton 1–2 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=25 May 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref> Rice became the 50th different player to start a Premier League game as captain for the Gunners.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL AFC"/> Tierney opened the scoring on 43 minutes with a near-post finish.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6372810/2025/05/25/southampton-1-arsenal-2-kieran-tierney-david-raya-martin-odegaard/ |title=Southampton 1 Arsenal 2 – Tierney signs off in style but more set-piece struggles |last1=McNicholas |first1=James |last2=Sheldon |first2=Dan |date=25 May 2025 |website=The New York Times |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref> In the 56th minute, [[Ross Stewart (footballer, born 1996)|Ross Stewart]] netted a header from a corner to draw the hosts level.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4316773 |title=Odegaard's late winner earns Arsenal victory at Southampton |date=25 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref> The goal meant that Arsenal had conceded 22 times from set pieces in all competitions this season.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL NYT"/> Despite conceding, Raya won the [[Premier League Golden Glove]] for the second consecutive season, sharing the award with Nottingham Forest goalkeeper [[Matz Sels]] who also had 13 clean sheets this campaign.<ref name="PL Golden Glove"/> Substitute Ødegaard rifled home from distance on 90 minutes, helping the Gunners win 2–1.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/southampton-vs-arsenal/report/506184 |title=Southampton 1–2 Arsenal: Martin Odegaard scores winner as Gunners break record for consecutive final-day victories |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=25 May 2025 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref> This was the 14th straight victory for Arsenal on the final day, breaking the record for the most consecutive top-flight season-enders won in English league history, which had stood for 101 years.<ref name="SOU v ARS PL SkySports"/> The result confirmed the Gunners' third straight second-place finish, marking the fifth time in English top-flight history that a team had been runners-up three years in a row, with Arsenal the first side to do so twice (also between [[1998–99 Arsenal F.C. season|1998–99]] and [[2000–01 Arsenal F.C. season|2000–01]]).<ref name="SOU v ARS PL"/> Arsenal didn't concede more than twice in any of their 58 games in all competitions this campaign, becoming the third Premier League side to have gone through an entire season without conceding three or more goals in a match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4321308 |title=The Wrap: What happened on the final day |last=Bloom |first=Ben |date=26 May 2025 |website=Premier League |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref>

===June===
Eleven Arsenal players (excluding loaned out players) were named in their respective countries' senior squads for international fixtures in June: Trossard (Belgium), Martinelli (Brazil), Lewis-Skelly, Rice and Saka (England), Ødegaard (as Norway's captain), Kiwior (Poland), Tierney (Scotland), Merino and Raya (Spain) and Zinchenko (Ukraine).<ref name="Intl call-ups Jun 2025 AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/duo-go-nations-league-glory-12-called |title=Duo go for Nations League glory as 12 called up |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2 Jun 2025 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Jun 2025}}</ref>
